talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning Accelerating Threat Triage with FortiSOAR-8.0 Agentic AI & MCP Integration.
talks.summary:
Overview: Fortinet demonstrates FortiSOAR 8.0's agentic AI and MCP integration for accelerating SOC threat triage through automated investigation workflows.

Key Topics: FortiAI configuration and token allocation; MCP server connectivity for extending agent capabilities; organization context for guiding investigations; and automated verdict generation with remediation recommendations.

Technical Details: AI agents query MCP-connected tools to enrich alerts with user details, process context, and IP/host intelligence. Agents evaluate evidence against organizational SOPs and deliver investigation summaries within seconds.

Takeaways: Agentic AI can eliminate repetitive triage when integrated with organizational context via MCP. SOC teams should evaluate AI agents that ground decisions in institutional knowledge.

talks.title: Baiada Poultry Strengthens Security, Visibility, and Operational Resilience with Fortinet
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning Baiada Poultry Strengthens Security, Visibility, and Operational Resilience with Fortinet.
talks.summary:
Business Requirements

Baiada Poultry executives describe a fast-paced food business where seconds matter—feedmill weighbridge outages can queue trucks for kilometers. Continuity of supply and customer service drive operational priorities.

Network Segmentation Goals

The company engaged Fortinet initially to segment the network, isolating manufacturing and operational components so a compromise in one bubble does not cascade across the environment.

Deployment and Partnership

A full architecture overhaul deployed Fortinet firewalls and switches suited to harsh manufacturing conditions, implemented with partner RP Glass whose engineers provided global Fortinet expertise.

Operational Outcomes

Post-deployment benefits include improved segmentation, enhanced security visibility with logs fed to their SOC, reduced risk, better availability and redundancy, eliminated network bottlenecks, and a stable platform for future growth with faster incident triage and traffic control.

talks.title: The Production vs Security Myth | OT Security
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of The Production vs Security Myth | OT Security.
talks.summary:
The Cultural Divide

Fortinet’s Nate Dan interviews OT specialist Fabio Piam about the persistent belief that plant security and production uptime cannot coexist. Fabio says the myth comes from past IT-led projects that disrupted operations and left lasting scars with operators who measure success in availability.

Different Security Priorities

OT teams prioritize availability of cyber-physical systems, while IT emphasizes confidentiality and integrity of data. Cyber initiatives must be co-designed with plant stakeholders or they are treated as operational risk rather than protection.

Flat Networks and Risk

Fabio warns that flat OT networks let one compromised device reach every process. Mixed brownfield assets—old, unpatched, and critical—need zone-based risk assessment under IEC 62443 rather than uniform treatment.

Segmentation Without Chaos

Good OT segmentation protects manufacturing KPIs: availability, performance, and quality. IT teams assisting segmentation must understand that changes which cause unplanned downtime or scrap undermine the business case for security.

talks.title: How Zaxby’s Secures 1,000+ Restaurant Locations with Fortinet | Customer Stories
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of How Zaxby’s Secures 1,000+ Restaurant Locations with Fortinet | Customer Stories.
talks.summary:
Company context

Zaxby's QSR leaders Jeremy Bargainer and Adam Price describe ~300 corporate staff, ~30,000 franchise-associated people, 1,000+ stores, rapid growth after Goldman Sachs/Leonard Green acquisition, and a four-person security team serving the whole brand.

Security journey

Post-acquisition, they built digital customer platforms and security from scratch. Fortinet became the backbone: FortiGate for store/franchise connectivity, FortiCNAT for cloud workloads, then FortiSIEM replacing an under-delivering prior SIEM, and FortiSOAR for automation and a single incident pane.

Franchise packaging

They offer franchisees a turnkey FortiGate/FortiAP/LTE-backup package so operators can focus on selling chicken, not networking.

Why Fortinet

Consolidation, native integrations, CMDB capabilities, mixing performance and security alerts, professional-services support for a fast SIEM migration, and planned AI use for defensive SOC assistance and guardrails against unsafe AI uploads.

talks.title: Protecting the Pitch & the Fairway: A Cybersecurity Conversation with Juventus and the DP World Tour
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of Protecting the Pitch & the Fairway: A Cybersecurity Conversation with Juventus and the DP World Tour.
talks.summary:
## Sports, Different Venues, Shared Risks

Fortinet hosts Juventus FC and DP World Tour executives at the club's Torino training complex for a cybersecurity roundtable. Football and golf differ operationally—fixed stadiums versus roaming tournaments—but both manage global brands, live broadcast infrastructure, athlete data, and fan-facing digital services under intense public scrutiny.

## Operational Security Challenges

Juventus operates corporate offices, training grounds, a player hotel, and a Fortinet-protected medical center handling sensitive health records. DP World Tour staff rebuild tournament IT from templates at each venue: inside the ropes they control systems; outside, promoters manage setup within mandated security footprints.

## Events as Temporary Critical Infrastructure

Concerts and major matches transform venues into high-density network environments where "secure right first time" replaced iterative fixes. Stakeholders—players, staff, broadcasters, attendees—expect invisible protection enabling performance without disruption.

## Security Driving Innovation

Participants reject treating security as mere compliance overhead. Protecting medical data, broadcast feeds, and commercial platforms enables innovation in fan engagement and athlete performance analytics. Cross-sport dialogue surfaces common patterns: global teams, third-party promoters, and perimeter assumptions that fail when responsibility extends beyond permanent facilities.

talks.title: Ganahl Lumber Simplifies Network Management with Fortinet | Customers
talks.teaser: An IT manager explains how templated, centrally managed Fortinet gear simplified a multi-site network run by a small team.
talks.summary:
Andy Takis, IT manager at Ganahl Lumber, describes how his company reworked its network after moving onto Fortinet products. Ganahl is a California lumber yard and hardware business founded in 1884, with 14 locations across Los Angeles, Orange County, Riverside and San Diego. Its yards range from about 2 to 20 acres of mostly outdoor space, where wood blocks wireless signals and access points are hard to place.

Before the rollout, the network was fragmented. Configurations were applied manually at each site, some switches had no passwords, and FortiGate perimeter devices ran alongside a separate SD-WAN product that was hard to get routing and interoperating. Troubleshooting was difficult. The current setup uses FortiGate firewalls and FortiSwitch switches, all managed through FortiManager with FortiAnalyzer, so the whole environment now sits in one place.

A very small team now relies on templated configurations, which make site rollouts far simpler. Takis presents simplicity and consistency as core design principles. His argument is that they let the team work proactively rather than constantly fighting fires when every location is set up differently.

talks.title: TVNZ BNZ Business Breakfast Interview | Fortinet
talks.teaser: Covers New Zealand's move from voluntary to mandatory cyber standards and why governance must go beyond compliance.
talks.summary:
Nicole Henry, who leads governance for Fortinet in Australia and New Zealand, discusses how artificial intelligence and automation are speeding up cyber threats. She describes a government cyber showcase she attended, where the discussion centred on getting governance settings right so that industry is prepared and able to respond.

On regulation, she contrasts the two countries. Australia moved quickly to set up its regulatory settings, while New Zealand has historically relied on a voluntary approach. The current consultation proposes clearer minimum mandatory standards. She puts the cost of cybercrime to the New Zealand economy at around 1.6 billion dollars a year and argues that these settings protect both national security and economic productivity.

She also argues that cybersecurity cannot be treated as a tick-box compliance exercise. Settings should support education, preparation and clear reporting so that organisations and citizens can react during a crisis. She says the consultation showed broad support despite some points of tension, and that New Zealand is drawing on several international models rather than copying Australia. Her takeaway for practitioners is that governance rules should be tailored to the local context.

talks.title: What's New in FortiOS 8.0 | Product Overview
talks.teaser: Shows how FortiOS 8.0 adds AI assistance, SaaS app classification, and SD-WAN app performance dashboards.
talks.summary:
This product overview introduces FortiOS 8.0, with AI as its central theme and a focus on both its benefits and its dangers. The headline addition is an AI assistant built into the firewall operating system, backed by an internal model and optional third-party models. Users describe what they need in natural language, search the product documentation, and apply the generated configuration to a FortiGate. The assistant can also help with more complex jobs such as VPN setup and can examine configurations and logs.

FortiView AI tracks AI services in use across the network. Administrators can block specific AI apps, for example ChatGPT, Claude, and Canva, through application control, and review session logs, chat messages, and risk ratings. Filters by use case, such as image generator or conversational assistant, plus session drill-downs show which accounts and data center locations are involved. Other changes include SaaS application tagging as sanctioned, approved, or unsanctioned, which overrides category-level rules; a new SD-WAN application performance dashboard showing latency, jitter, and packet loss; and custom tags that automatically place new address objects into dynamic groups.

The video closes with an example of FortiView's support for the Model Context Protocol, where a developer's GitHub connection from Visual Studio Code shows reviewed files, assigned issues, and repository updates in session detail. The main takeaway is finer control over which AI and SaaS applications users can reach, paired with per-session visibility.

talks.summary:
The presenters outline a partnership between Fortinet and HCL Tech across secure access service edge areas: network security, zero trust access, secure web gateways, endpoint security APIs, and OT–IT convergence. HCL contributes assessment, consulting, professional services, and managed services atop Fortinet’s portfolio so customers can adopt SASE shaped to their own requirements.

They describe aligned delivery principles: SASE design and advisory work, integration blueprints that plug into existing technology, and worldwide rollout that still meets regional compliance. They stress hybrid SASE—cloud plus on-premises—to support data sovereignty amid shifting political constraints, along with visibility, analytics, and automation to standardize operations, cut cost and complexity, and support digital transformation.

Future joint investment themes include AI-powered detection and response integrated into security operations, extending SASE beyond user-to-application access toward IoT and edge-to-cloud paths, and stronger emphasis on response and recovery—not only prevention. They close by positioning SASE as a consumable service whose scale can flex with how the organization uses the network.

talks.title: FortiSIEM Automation In Action | Product Demo
talks.teaser: Demonstrates a SIEM playbook that strips an unauthorized user from Domain Admins and disables the account automatically.
talks.summary:
This four-minute product demo from Fortinet walks through an automated response to a common privilege escalation scenario: a user being added to the Domain Admins group in Active Directory. The presenter explains that FortiSIEM keeps a lookup table of authorized administrators, and that any account outside that list is treated as a possible privilege escalation or a lingering threat once it is added.

To show detection, the presenter adds a test user to the group, then finds the resulting alert in the FortiSIEM console and opens its rule logic. The logic shows the event was flagged because the user was missing from the lookup table. The response playbook is then run, pulling the username from the incident and passing it to the Active Directory connector, which removes the account from the privileged group and disables it. The presenter checks Active Directory afterward to confirm the change, and a canvas view is shown that maps the playbook steps visually.

The rest of the demo covers the automation content library, which the presenter says offers over 700 connectors, and the playbook designer, where triggers such as application events, automation policies and FortiRecon can start a playbook. The video closes with pre-built remediation playbooks and an example that blocks a malicious IP address using a built-in connector. The takeaway is that a lookup-based check on privileged group changes can drive containment without manual steps.

talks.title: General Session: Robert May | Accelerate26
talks.teaser: Walks through a real incident response case at an OT company and the products that address its security gaps.
talks.summary:
Fortinet's executive vice president of product management opens the session by previewing three themes from the Tech Expo: data sovereignty, AI adoption, and cyber resiliency. He frames recurring gaps that the FortiGuard incident response team sees on customer sites, including poor visibility, weak security hygiene, alert overload, and products that are not connected into a platform.

He then walks through one incident response case at an operational technology company. The breach came through remote access, and responders used FortiNDR Cloud to find that the attacker had moved laterally. Their report gave five recommendations. Contractor access was to be restricted with FortiSASE and its secure browser, which limits sessions to a vetted browser and can block screenshots, copy and paste, and printing. Deception devices were proposed for OT segments. An SSPM with a GenAI feature was suggested to generate checks for unsanctioned SaaS apps without waiting for code updates. Shadow AI was addressed with FortiOS 8.0 dashboards, which flagged DeepSeek traffic to China and a developer's upload of source code containing credentials that triggered a DLP violation.

The last two recommendations were DLP, added to an existing FortiClient installer rather than a new agent, and a SOC that was overloaded with alerts. For the SOC, the speaker described FortiSOC, a SaaS offering built on FortiAnalyzer, FortiSIEM and FortiSOAR, with agentic AI that investigated a blocked SQL injection alert and escalated it. The talk closes by separating AI used for security from security for AI, and points attendees to booths and breakout sessions for details.

talks.title: General Session: Derek Manky, Carl Windsor, WEF | Accelerate26
talks.teaser: A panel unpacks the World Economic Forum's latest cybersecurity outlook, contrasting CEO and CISO priorities amid AI-driven threats.
talks.summary:
The session opens with a montage on collapsing exploit windows, cybercrime-as-a-service, and the need for intelligence plus public–private collaboration. Fortinet’s threat intelligence lead frames an unprecedented pace of change, wider attack surfaces, and new actors drawn into fraud and scam operations.

Julia Masketta summarizes the fifth Global Cybersecurity Outlook from the World Economic Forum’s Center for Cybersecurity: survey data shows AI as the dominant driver of change, rising pre-deployment security reviews, geopolitics reshaping strategy for most large firms, cyber-enabled fraud touching most respondents and topping CEO concerns ahead of ransomware, and supply-chain risk blocking resilience for many organizations. Carl Windsor describes how generative AI spreads inside business units without guardrails, accelerates adversary tooling such as agent frameworks sold on criminal markets, and pushes CISOs toward resilience and board-level narratives on quantum transition and diversified sourcing.

The panel contrasts executive versus security-leadership worries, then covers product-security practices under faster exploitation, including transparency, hardening, virtual patching, and enforced multifactor authentication. Closing takeaways stress cross-sector collaboration to disrupt crime and disciplined attack-surface reduction through discovery, documentation, and patching.

A Fortinet-led general session brings together senior technology leaders from Lowe's and Waste Management to compare large-scale security and networking transformations. The discussion frames replacement decisions less around feature checklists and more around vendor trust, long-term operating models, and execution when incidents matter.

Waste Management describes edge firewalls that classify north-south traffic into OT, secure employee and vendor access, and consolidate management across thousands of acquired sites. The team stresses strict IT/OT separation, cross-functional systems thinking, and moving bespoke sites toward standardized lanes for IoT, internet, and SCADA workloads. Near-term priorities include asset visibility through an identity center, PLC identification, policy hardening, and OT telemetry integrated into enterprise monitoring while keeping operations simple for junior staff.

Lowe's emphasizes environmental consistency, automation at scale, and predictability as the business accelerates faster than security can traditionally keep pace. Guidance for similar programs starts with how the organization wants to operate, defines a trust model for products and partners, and pilots change in repeatable areas first. Looking ahead, Lowe's ties networking and security work to customer and associate experience, engineer focus, and operational repeatability, including an internal AI assistant aimed at reducing DIY project revisits.

On SASE, he claimed lower costs from Fortinet's own data centers, easy migration for existing firewall and SD-WAN customers, and sovereign, on-premises, cloud and colocation options. For AI security, he described coverage across five layers, from chips and infrastructure to models and applications, and said AI-enabled operations can cut response time. talks.title: FortiPAM SSH and Windows Application Filtering | Product Demo
talks.teaser: Shows how FortiPAM blocks risky SSH commands and restricts Windows executables like mstsc.exe during privileged sessions.
talks.summary:
Greg Genta presents two ways FortiPAM reduces risk during privileged sessions. The first is SSH command filtering, which lets an administrator block specific commands on a per-session basis instead of handing over a full shell. The example given is stopping factory reset commands on a network device, so that one mistake does not become an outage. Enforcement happens inline during the session, with logging for audit purposes.

The second is Windows application filtering for RDP sessions. FortiPAM pushes a policy over WinRM to the target Windows server, scoped to a specific user and session, that allows or blocks named executables. The use case shown is preventing lateral movement: blocking the Windows remote desktop client, mstsc.exe, so a user cannot jump from one server into another.

In the live demo, a standard user checks out a stored secret and opens a PuTTY session to a FortiGate. Commands on the blocked list, including a ping and execute factory reset, are refused with a message to check with the administrator. The admin then reviews those blocked commands in the SSH audit log. In the RDP part, launching mstsc from inside the session is stopped by the application filter. The takeaway is that session-scoped controls can keep approved administrators within their assigned tasks without broad access.

The session is a checklist for operators planning upgrades rather than a threat-modeling deep dive.

talks.title: FortiSIEM 7.5 Agentic AI | Product Demo
talks.teaser: Shows FortiSIEM 7.5's AI assistant triaging incidents, building investigations, and generating SQL-backed threat hunting queries.
talks.summary:
This product demo presents the agentic AI capabilities added in FortiSIEM 7.5, framed as an assistant that helps a security operations center automate triage, plan investigations and speed up root cause analysis. It starts from the incident list, where an analyst filters by a malware rule and opens an incident in agentic analysis mode. The incident triage agent builds an investigation plan, runs the queries, adjusts its analysis based on the results and summarizes the whole investigation. From there, the findings can be exported as a PDF or pushed into a new case, where the analysis stays in the case notes for the assigned analyst.

The second part looks at user risk. Asking the assistant about a specific user returns an aggregated profile. A prompt library offers predefined agentic prompts, and the presenter chooses one that lists the incidents a user is involved in, grouped by severity and ranked from high to low with match counts. For proactive hunting, a natural-language request for inbound traffic from outside the US over the last hour returns a visualization, along with the SQL query the assistant generated. That query can be copied to the analytics tab and run in advanced search for further refinement.

The takeaway is that AI-generated investigation plans, case notes and visible query logic can shorten the path from detection to deep-dive analysis. Because the underlying SQL is exposed, analysts can check what the assistant produced and refine it themselves.

talks.title: FortiPAM Integration with Fortinet IAM Solutions | Products
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how FortiPAM combines with FortiAuthenticator and FortiIdentity Cloud for privileged access and MFA.
talks.summary:
### Overview
In this demonstration, Jannar Garcia, Technical Marketing Engineer at Fortinet, presents an identity and access management (IAM) architecture integrating FortiPAM (privileged access management), FortiAuthenticator Cloud, and FortiIdentity Cloud. The solution addresses challenges faced by enterprises of any size and MSSPs—especially during mergers and acquisitions—when unifying disparate identity providers and managing access for diverse user categories, such as contractors and employees.

### Key Topics
- **Role-Tailored Dashboards**: Providing streamlined dashboards with pre-selected targets for contractors and robust, feature-rich dashboards for full employees.
- **Unified Identity Federation**: Integrating FortiPAM with FortiAuthenticator Cloud to support third-party IdPs such as Entra ID, Okta, Active Directory, or local authentication.
- **Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)**: Leveraging FortiIdentity Cloud to enforce MFA via mobile push notifications (FortiToken Mobile) or email verification to mitigate phishing and credential compromise.
- **Access Control & Segmentation**: Using direct connections for internal users and ZTNA (referred to in transcript as CTNA/C10A) tagging controls for remote endpoints.
- **Auditing and Session Recording**: Capturing granular logs, recording user sessions, tracking commands entered, and generating access and launcher reports.

### Technical Details
- **Authentication Workflow**: When users authenticate to FortiPAM, FortiAuthenticator Cloud validates credentials against a remote user database via RADIUS or SAML. FortiIdentity Cloud subsequently enforces MFA.
- **Configuration & Launchers**: Remote users (such as `Carl at octa.com` and `JDO`) are configured with SAML and delivery options like FortiToken via mobile or email activation. During testing, various access sessions are launched, including SSH via PuTTY, WinSCP, Web SSH, Web SFTP, and Remote Desktop/Web RDP to targets such as `customer 2 Windows server`.
- **Auto-Provisioning**: FortiPAM features auto-provisioning, which automatically generates privileges and grants access to secrets.
- **Monitoring & Reporting**: FortiPAM logs connection metadata—including date, source IP, destination IP, secret server name, user, and launcher type. In addition to recording the actual session and commands executed, administrators can export general reports, user login reports, system reports, and secret launcher reports from the management portal.

### Takeaways
The combination of FortiPAM, FortiAuthenticator Cloud, and FortiIdentity Cloud provides a unified IAM and PAM framework. It simplifies identity management across mixed identity providers while enforcing least privilege, zero-trust endpoint tagging, multi-factor authentication, and comprehensive session auditing.

talks.title: FortiCamera Cloud: People and Face Detection | Product Demo
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how FortiCamera Cloud sets up people counting, face search and cross-camera person tracking.
talks.summary:
This short product demo from Fortinet shows how the people and face detection features of FortiCamera Cloud are configured in a camera's detection settings. The first feature is a people analytic that counts individuals entering or exiting an area or crossing a line. The demo places a crossing line at a building's front entrance, adjusts its endpoints by dragging them, and then shows how many people come in or go out and the premises' occupancy across the day.

The next part covers searching for a person by attributes. The presenter filters for a man wearing a hat with a black main upper garment and opens a thumbnail to view that recording. Face detection works similarly: a search over a chosen time window lists every detected face with its recordings, and a selected face can be used to narrow results to one individual. A person-of-interest view then lists anyone recorded on a given camera.

The video closes with the activity search section, which applies the same search tools across several cameras. Selecting the cameras lets a viewer follow a person of interest through each one within a chosen period, which the demo presents as useful for tracing where someone matching given attributes appeared. Viewers come away with a clear picture of what the cloud camera product can do with people data and how its analytics are set up.

talks.title: From ‘Not My Problem’ to Critical Priority: How Cities Are Taking Control of OT | OT Security
talks.teaser: An IT director explains how his city took over water SCADA oversight, segmented legacy OT networks, and leaned on neighboring cities.
talks.summary:
A municipal IT director describes how his city stepped in to oversee water SCADA systems that had long been run by operations staff and vendors with little IT involvement. These systems were often left unpatched for years and were plugged into flat data networks without security or compliance review, so the IT team took responsibility for them and worked with the water utility to set rules everyone would follow.

For segmentation, the city separates each division and function from the others and uses Fortinet equipment to give people access only to what their jobs require. He gives the example of a concession stand at a water park, whose staff should never be able to reach the OT network. Logs of blocked attempts show who is trying to get in, which helps staff decide whether an event is an incident, a mistake or curiosity. For the controllers themselves, the guiding mindset is to assume a PLC is insecure, leave it unchanged, build a boundary around it, monitor it, and block any behavior outside its expected function, bringing in a trusted SCADA vendor to review anything suspicious.

The talk closes on collaboration. Neighboring city IT directors share incident details and fixes, and existing agreements let cities borrow staff during large-scale incidents, which matters for a small department. The overall takeaway is to treat any new system as potentially insecure, build defenses around it, and rely on peer cities for backup.

talks.title: Agentic AI Is Coming - Is Your SOC Ready? | Interview
talks.teaser: Covers AI-accelerated attacks, SOC integration challenges and collective efforts against cybercrime rings.
talks.summary:
AI-enabled tools are speeding up attacks, shrinking the window for response and making attackers more targeted, particularly in the second half of the year. In Asia Pacific, manufacturing remains the most-hit sector, followed by healthcare and digital government services, while mobile devices are increasingly seen as weak links. The discussion stresses integration, since organizations often run 40 to 50 or more security tools, and IT and OT teams working in separate streams can miss events that cross between them.

On defense, AI is presented as a necessity for security operations centers, helping analysts upskill, cutting operating costs and shortening response to seconds or minutes, while attackers are seen as only beginning to adopt it. Customers judge value through metrics such as threats mitigated and average response time. Practical controls include MFA moving toward zero trust, because stolen or phished credentials still drive many attacks. Maturity is described in levels, from basic visibility and integration to playbook-driven operations and deception environments. Securing AI systems, data privacy and governance are named as next challenges.

Collective defense is illustrated by a cybercrime initiative under the World Economic Forum and law enforcement work. Operation Serengeti led to over a thousand arrests and about $45 million recovered for victims, while Operation Serengeti 2.0 produced 1,200 arrests and $90 million recovered. The outlook points to wider OT attacks and autonomous AI agents that might find vulnerabilities, write proof-of-concept exploits or sell compromised access, with continuous threat exposure management offered as a response.

talks.title: AI, OT, and the Rise of Shared Cyber Accountability | Interview
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for AI, OT, and the Rise of Shared Cyber Accountability | Interview.

talks.title: High Availability Options in an 5G/LTE Environment | Overview
talks.teaser: Compares single-modem carrier switching with dual-modem failover for LTE and 5G links, using live ping tests and health checks.
talks.summary:
Cellular WAN links are now common enough to serve as primary connections for remote sites, vehicles and field devices, not just as backups. This talk compares two ways to build failover on LTE and 5G gear: a dual-carrier setup on one modem versus a platform with two modems. The speaker starts with the architecture, noting that each modem holds two SIMs but can connect to only one carrier at a time, because switching carriers requires loading a different firmware image and rebooting the modem.

In the single-modem demo, a manual carrier switch dropped a continuous ping stream. The speaker lost 54 pings, about 4 and a half minutes with a 5-second timeout, which shows how slow a modem reload is. That makes this approach suitable for rare events such as a tower outage, a nearly exhausted data plan, or a utility truck working far from its home region. The dual-modem demo then failed over to the second carrier with a 1-second timeout, losing at most about one ping and sometimes showing a latency change. The speaker walked through the virtual WAN configuration, which keeps traffic on the higher-priority member until health checks on loss, latency or jitter mark it unhealthy.

The key difference is visibility. With two modems, health checks can run continuously on both carriers, so the system can choose the best link at any moment. A single modem has no performance data on its standby carrier. Layer 3 failover can be sub-second, but the speaker warned that some applications react poorly to path changes, so thresholds must be tuned to avoid unnecessary switching between carriers. The takeaway is to match the design to the outage tolerance and the behaviour of the applications that depend on the link.

talks.title: FortiSIEM
talks.teaser: Armis Integration | Product Demo details FortiSIEM.
talks.summary:
### Overview
This presentation demonstrates the real-time integration between FortiSIEM and Armis, illustrating how combining the two platforms establishes an automated, comprehensive security ecosystem. Armis supplies asset intelligence and context, while FortiSIEM utilizes this data to power a unified Configuration Management Database (CMDB), enhanced threat correlation analytics, and automated response capabilities.

### Key Topics
- **Credential Setup and API Connection**: Establishing integration between FortiSIEM and Armis using REST API keys under the admin settings.
- **Asset Discovery and Synchronization**: Pulling asset information discovered by Armis directly into FortiSIEM to populate and classify devices in the CMDB.
- **Event Ingestion and Health Verification**: Monitoring integration health via event status checks and reviewing 24-hour event reports.
- **Threat Correlation and Incident Detection**: Aggregating disparate alerts from Armis into a coherent attack sequence within FortiSIEM.
- **Investigation and Response Automation**: Expanding threat context using visual investigation features and addressing incidents via automation playbooks and dedicated IoT/OT dashboards.

### Technical Details
- **Integration Configuration**: In the admin section under setup and credentials, a REST API key is configured to establish the connection with Armis.
- **Asset Classification in CMDB**: Asset scans directly pull devices into FortiSIEM, with discovery results logged in the history log. Filtering the CMDB by the Armis REST API method shows that FortiSIEM automatically categorizes discovered hardware, including IT and IoT devices.
- **Event Ingestion**: The pull events interface verifies connection health with a green check mark, and 24-hour reports show event types generated by Armis.
- **Alert Correlation**: In a demonstrated scenario, Armis flags several individual alerts originating from source IP `192.168.86.67`—including communication to an external host, communication to a suspicious host, and a Chinese DNS query. FortiSIEM correlates these discrete alerts into a single actionable incident representing the complete attack chain.
- **Investigation Workflow**: The investigation tab reveals that `192.168.86.67` belongs to a printer. Further visual investigation exposes that the same printer attempted an Active Directory logon and communicated with a malicious FortiGuard-flagged IP address located in China.
- **Dashboarding and Remediation**: Threats can be mitigated using FortiSIEM automation playbooks. Additionally, the FortiSIEM OT/IoT dashboard contains a dedicated Armis section displaying real-time alerts, host-triggered events, device details, associated CVEs, and alert policies.

### Takeaways
The integration allows security teams to automatically discover and classify unmanaged IT and IoT assets, correlate fragmented alerts into end-to-end attack chains, perform deep visual investigations, and trigger automated remediation playbooks directly within FortiSIEM.

talks.title: FortiGate Cloud Management and Analytics Platform | Network Security
talks.teaser: Shows a cloud portal for managing many FortiGate firewalls at once, with logs, reports and alerts.
talks.summary:
The talk starts with the problem of managing enterprise networks made up of many FortiGate firewalls, switches, access points and extenders, often spread across separate security fabrics. Administrators must push policies and security profiles to each unit, and every device has its own web interface, so operators log in to each one separately. The presenter introduces FortiGate Cloud as a hosted service that aims to simplify this work across single deployments and larger customer footprints.

The demo walks through the portal. After signing in, users see every FortiGate registered to their account, shown on a map or in a groupable list, and can add devices by entering a cloud key or provisioning them from the list. Customizable dashboards report general information, network health, security status and SD-WAN monitoring. A remote access view opens the standard FortiGate interface in real time, and from there administrators can schedule configuration backups, manage firmware updates and send files to the sandbox.

Logs are kept for up to a year, so administrators can download raw logs and study historical trends. Reports can be generated automatically with quick filters showing how applications, websites, users and threats affect the network, and email alerts notify staff of important events as they happen. For managed security providers, an organization dashboard lists tenant accounts, devices and licenses. One access point covers every connected device, cutting IT staff time.

talks.title: SD-WAN Overlay-as-a-Service Powered by FortiGate Cloud Advanced Service | Products
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how a FortiGate Cloud service builds an SD-WAN overlay between branch sites and applies one shared policy.
talks.summary:
This short demo introduces Overlay-as-a-Service, a turnkey SD-WAN option within FortiGate Cloud Advanced that connects corporate and cloud locations through a single cloud portal. Setup begins by choosing two Fortinet-hosted hub locations, Plano in Texas and Vancouver in Canada, with the second hub kept for redundancy. Each site is then defined by its FortiGate device, its internet links and its local subnets. The presenter builds a headquarters site and branch sites in Chicago and New York this way.

Once the overlay is pushed, the topology page shows each site's tunnel status, which appears orange until the VPN tunnel comes up. Generating traffic between hosts on two subnets triggers a shortcut tunnel through Fortinet's ADVPN technology, and a ping test between the Sunnyvale and Chicago subnets confirmed one. For policy, the presenter groups all local subnets into a single address object and creates one overlay policy that allows all traffic between sites with IPS enabled. That policy is then applied to every FortiGate in the overlay.

Looking at one FortiGate afterward shows that the service created several local policies from that single intent-based rule. The presenter said the New York site showed a similar result, with four policies on each site. The takeaway is that a few inputs per site can produce a working, monitored site-to-site overlay, and the time saved grows with each site added.

talks.title: Starting Strong: Cybersecurity for Utilities | OT Security
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Starting Strong: Cybersecurity for Utilities | OT Security.

talks.title: Smart Buildings: Where Cybersecurity Meets Sustainability | Industries
talks.teaser: Explores why connected building systems need security planning alongside sustainability goals and what risks they bring.
talks.summary:
Matt Bolic and Meera Ramanathan open a conversation about how security and sustainability overlap in connected buildings. Ramanathan explains that smart buildings monitor nearly everything, from energy use to window blinds, so they work like large digital devices whose disruption could affect the people who work or live inside them.

They then walk through the risks they see. A single building can produce over 10,000 data points, which raises privacy concerns about employee check-ins and energy consumption. Building management systems, which run on IoT and sit at the core of a smart building, are so interconnected that responders may have to untangle many links to find where an attack started. They also note that no cybersecurity protocol exists specifically for smart buildings, even as HVAC, fire safety, elevators, entry doors and signage join the building network.

Ramanathan argues that facilities staff, third-party vendors and other groups running a building may not know how to stop such attacks, so education is a key task for security professionals. Using an elevator example, she shows how a single fault can involve safety, energy and people-management systems linked together. Her advice to sustainability leaders is to bring cybersecurity specialists into smart building projects from the start, so they can understand likely attack paths and limit impact on both occupants and the environment.

talks.title: Incident Preparedness & Response (Zero Trust Mindset) | Industries
talks.teaser: Maps common water-utility intrusions and SSL VPN weak points, then ties zero trust, segmentation, and tabletops to real response.
talks.summary:
The conversation centers on incident patterns affecting water utilities and broader critical infrastructure. Financially motivated ransomware dominates, often hitting small and midsize operators with limited security staff and budgets. Attackers frequently enter through public-facing weaknesses, with SSL VPN vulnerabilities standing out; across investigated cases in 2024, roughly half of initial accesses involved exploitation of internet-exposed applications. After entry, weak segmentation allows lateral movement and privilege escalation that can reach operational technology, not only IT.

Preparation emphasizes patching and hardening remote access, enforcing multifactor authentication, micro-segmenting IT from OT, and validating that separation through tests rather than assumptions. Regular tabletop exercises are framed as essential because a utility ransomware event spans operations, legal, communications, and leadership. During an active incident, a zero trust posture means no blanket access for responders or admins, just-in-time and least-privilege access (including read-only investigative use of security tools), network segmentation and firewall rules to limit blast radius, automated isolation where appropriate, and full auditability of access and actions for post-incident review.

A recurring response failure is trusting theoretical OT air gaps that prove porous via jump servers, shared credentials, vendor paths, or ad hoc remote access. For resource-constrained utilities, the advised sequence is a readiness assessment to surface existing informal practices and gaps, then an outline covering ownership, escalation, critical systems, and priorities before formal documentation, followed by practical tabletop drills. The plan need not be lengthy but must match real people, tools, and environments.

talks.title: FortiPAM Demo | Privileged Access Management
talks.teaser: Delivers a FortiPAM demo of bastion access with approvals, session recording, four modes, ZTNA checks, and reverse gateways.
talks.summary:
The presentation introduces FortiPAM as Fortinet’s privileged access management offering, positioned as a centralized bastion or jump server for elevated accounts and sensitive systems. It can run as a virtual machine on premises, in public cloud, or as hardware. Users authenticate into FortiPAM before reaching protected “secrets” such as RDP, SSH, or HTTPS administrative sessions. The speaker outlines layered approval workflows, full session recording for audit and forensics, automated password and SSH key rotation, Windows service password updates, exclusive time-bound secret checkout, SSH command filtering, and live session monitoring with termination and log download.

Four access modes are compared, each with sessions recorded: agentless browser launchers for web RDP, SSH, and VNC; a browser extension for HTTPS GUI proxy secrets; a free FortiClient for native tools like PuTTY and RDP; and FortiClient integrated with FortiEMS and ZTNA for device posture tags and client certificate checks. A distributed gateway section explains forward connections from the central server versus reverse gateways that maintain outbound polls so publicly hosted FortiPAM can reach segmented networks without inbound holes.

The live demonstration walks a contractor via agentless SSH and RDP, shows GUI secrets requiring the plugin, uses FortiClient with secret checkout via PuTTY, submits a timed RDP access request with ticket context and admin approval, denies ZTNA login from an unenrolled machine, connects through a colleague’s reverse gateway to remote lab RDP, and reviews downloadable session video plus SSH command logs. Practitioners see how the product bundles vaulting behavior, accountability controls, and segmented access patterns in one console.

talks.title: FortiPAM Demo | Privileged Access Management
talks.teaser: Attendees see FortiPAM agentless access, extensions, client checkout, approvals, ZTNA, reverse tunnels, and command plus video audit.
talks.summary:
The session walks through FortiPAM as privileged access for contractors and employees who reach secrets through local or federated login, often with MFA. It opens with agentless connectivity: browser-based SSH to a FortiGate firewall and RDP to Windows, both with a visible recording indicator while commands run in the session. Agentless access does not cover GUI or HTTPS proxy-pass secrets; those require a browser extension that installs from the store, fills credentials, proxies the connection, and still records activity.

A separate path uses the free FortiClient for FortiPAM to launch secrets with native tools such as PuTTY, including checkout that temporarily exclusives a secret. The demo adds time-bound access requests with ticket notes, optional scheduled pre-approval, and administrator approval before RDP. Full FortiClient registered to EMS reaches FortiPAM through a ZTNA interface after certificate checks, while an unregistered contractor machine is denied. A reverse gateway links two environments so RDP reaches a remote lab server through an outbound tunnel brokered between FortiPAM instances.

Practitioners see centralized launch methods, enforcement at the ZTNA boundary, and audit depth: secret event video with fullscreen and download, plus per-secret SSH command history alongside recordings across agentless, extension, and client modes.

talks.title: Introduction to FortiIdentity Cloud and Features | Products
talks.teaser: Surveys the headline features of FortiIdentity Cloud's identity and access management service, from local IDP to identity proxy.
talks.summary:
This product video introduces FortiIdentity Cloud, a hosted identity and access management service managed through a web interface. It covers one-time passwords delivered through mobile and hardware tokens, SMS and email, plus passkey support, and it can provide multifactor authentication for Fortinet and third-party products, including through REST API integration. Native integrations with FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiSandbox and FortiADC are described as requiring no extra hardware or software.

The main feature covered in detail is the local identity provider, where users authenticate with credentials stored entirely inside the service rather than an external source such as Azure AD, Okta or Google. The presenter argues this reduces cost, complexity and privacy concerns, and suits organisations that put control or data sovereignty first. The service can also act as a SAML 2.0 identity provider and an OIDC provider, giving centralised single sign-on with consistent enforcement of policies such as MFA.

The video closes with two further features. Auto alias by email lets one user hold different usernames across applications while still being assigned a single token; it is enabled in the realm general settings, and alias users must belong to the same realm. The identity proxy sits between identity providers and service providers, acting as an IDP to SP and an SP to IDPs, so standard SSO integrations can be added and adaptive authentication applied without changes to downstream systems.

talks.title: Fireside Chat: Rethinking Cyber Risk with Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) | Products
talks.teaser: Explores how continuous threat exposure management maps external attack surfaces, brand risks and dark web activity for security leaders.
talks.summary:
The fireside chat opens with the CISO describing what keeps security leaders up at night: the unknown parts of a fast-changing attack surface, shaped by acquisitions, new technology and third-party suppliers. Continuous threat exposure management is presented as a framework that starts by seeing the organisation the way an attacker would, then ranks findings by the tactics real threat actors use instead of producing a long list of issues.

The conversation then turns to the vendor's FortiRecon platform, which combines external and internal attack surface assessment, brand protection covering phishing, exposed executive data, leaked code and misconfigured storage buckets, and dark web monitoring that gives early warning of attacks. The latest release adds an AI assistant that answers questions about threat actors and produces summaries for management, native web application scanning, and security automation. Examples include resetting leaked Office 365 credentials and opening escalation paths when an alert names the organisation, and feeding findings into web application firewall changes.

Real-world examples from executive briefings include assets customers did not know they had, critically vulnerable systems already being exploited, leaked user credentials that could enable credential stuffing, and stealer malware that the speaker said almost always turned up in scans. For banks and other firms with customers, stealer data can show where those customers are exposed. The most valuable finding during proofs of concept was initial access broker activity, which lets teams act before a compromise. The takeaway is that visibility into unknown exposure, paired with automation that shortens the window for exploitation, is the practical goal.

talks.title: FortiGate 700G: Unprecedented Performance with Fortinet’s 5th-Gen ASIC Security Processor | Products
talks.teaser: Presents FortiGate 700G throughput figures and a vendor-run security efficacy test with mixed HTTPS traffic.
talks.summary:
This vendor presentation introduces the FortiGate 700G, a firewall aimed at enterprise edge sites and distributed enterprises. The appliance offers separate management and high-availability ports, along with a mix of 5GB RJ45, 1GB SFP, 10GB SFP+ and 25GB SFP28 connections. Its SP5 content processor is described as offloading pattern and content matching from the main CPU.

An NP7 network processor provides hardware-accelerated security and networking. The stated figures are 164 Gbit per second of firewall throughput, 26 GB per second of threat protection, 16 million concurrent sessions, and SSL deep inspection at 14 Gbit per second. For the demo, the presenters ran a Breaking Point quick test built on an open, vendor-neutral test suite that measures throughput and security efficacy against known traffic and attack scenarios. With application control, antivirus, IPS and SSL deep inspection all enabled under high-security policies, a mixed HTTPS test reached about 14 Gbit per second of SSL deep inspection, while the IPS engines ran at roughly 80 to 90 percent CPU.

In the security efficacy section, the test was fast-forwarded, and the device earned a grade A across the suite. In the malware results, it blocked 3,838 of 3,930 attacks, also graded A. The main takeaway is that throughput numbers depend on which inspection features are enabled and on the traffic mix, so the reported results apply to this specific test setup.

talks.title: Introduction to FortiToken Cloud | Product Demos
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Introduction to FortiToken Cloud | Product Demos.

talks.title: Introduction to FortiToken Cloud | Products & Solutions
talks.teaser: Gives an overview of FortiToken Cloud's identity features, including local IDP, OpenID Provider support and shared tokens.
talks.summary:
The video introduces FortiToken Cloud as a web-based identity and access management service for securing identities and managing access. It covers the supported authentication methods, including mobile and hardware tokens, one-time passwords sent by SMS or email, and passwordless passkeys. It also outlines multifactor authentication across Fortinet and third-party devices, token sharing, realms for managed security providers, and adaptive authentication.

The main features are explained in turn. Local IDP lets users sign in with a username and password stored inside the service, without relying on an external provider such as Google, Azure or Okta, and multifactor authentication can still be layered on top. FortiToken Cloud can also act as an OpenID Connect provider, authenticating users and issuing tokens to relying parties. Paired with the local IDP, it becomes the authentication source and supports single sign-on. Shared tokens let a user with the same username or email reuse one token across applications in the same realm, while auto alias by email lets a user with different usernames across applications share a single token. That setting is enabled in the realm general settings.

The closing point is that the service can serve as an identity and access management solution for an organization. It offers native integration with Fortinet products without extra hardware or software, and it can add multifactor authentication to any web application through its REST API, SAML or OIDC. A practitioner would take away that a cloud-hosted token service can centralize login and MFA for both Fortinet and custom web apps, with local IDP and token sharing reducing reliance on external identity providers.

talks.title: FortiSIEM Product Overview | Product Demo
talks.teaser: Walks through FortiSIEM dashboards, incident triage, playbook automation and CMDB-driven log analytics in a product demo.
talks.summary:
The demo opens with FortiSIEM dashboards. A risk summary shows overall risk status, high-risk devices and users, and risk trend over time, while a middle panel lists active incidents and supports filtering and correlation. An EDR dashboard is filtered to one host, extended with reports chosen from more than 4,000 options, and a donut chart is switched to a Sankey graph. An out-of-the-box Office 365 dashboard fills once that integration is connected.

Incident views range from a top-incidents overview to a detailed risk view showing a timeline and placement on the MITRE ATT&CK IT and ICS frameworks. The presenter opens a malware-in-email incident that already has a case. The AI-generated case analysis covers timeline, sources, targets, attack chain and remediation, such as isolating the host and scanning the network. A single event triggered the incident.

A playbook selected by incident tags then runs. It asks the analyst to confirm blocking an IP address on a firewall, which is approved, and to block a user in Active Directory, which is declined. It then runs analytical queries and writes an incident report covering threat details, emails, a timeline and 51 unique recipients last Friday. Playbook steps appear in a canvas view, and playbooks can be built by drag and drop or taken from a content hub with over 675 connectors. It closes with the CMDB, which discovers and monitors devices, and a failed-login example that uses a predefined group limited to Windows servers, avoiding complex query language.

talks.title: Navigating AI, Misinformation & Cyber Resilience with Orange Cyberdefense | Fortinet ON AIR
talks.teaser: A service provider executive discusses how generative AI fuels attacks, deepfake fraud and the need for agile, sustainable defenses.
talks.summary:
The conversation, recorded live at MWC 2025, opens with a guest from Orange Cyberdefense on the emerging technologies worrying defenders. The guest sees AI as both an offensive tool and a defensive opportunity, citing the company's Security Navigator report on attacker use. The most visible risk is generative AI making it hard to separate true from false content, which fuels social engineering and deepfake voice fraud. Attacks on AI systems themselves are expected too, since models with broad data access will attract attackers as they are built into products.

Defence is framed as a race against time: the aim is to shrink the gap between an attack and its detection. Automation, now boosted by generative AI, could help with detection, remediation and patch prioritisation. A Fortinet participant notes its long use of supervised machine learning and the need to validate samples so training data is not poisoned. The guest adds that staff need training, including on prompt engineering, and that security should be designed in from the start rather than bolted on after rollout.

The closing segment covers agility and supply chains. Since rankings of language models shift weekly, the guest advises against relying on a single solution and recommends diversifying suppliers, including for threat intelligence, so dependencies stay sustainable. Existing outsourcing and cloud controls can be extended to AI, while models should be protected as valuable assets that could be stolen. The episode ends with plans for a follow-up next year.

talks.title: 's Lacework FortiCNAPP for Google Cloud | Demo
talks.teaser: Shows how FortiCNAPP ranks exploitable cloud vulnerabilities and combines weak signals into high-priority attack alerts.
talks.summary:
This short product demo walks through FortiCNAPP, a cloud security platform meant to bring development, cloud configuration and runtime protection into one view. The presenter argues that code repositories hide many vulnerabilities, that cloud services carry dozens of settings where one mistake can expose data, and that identities often hold far more privileges than they use. The platform is presented as giving developers early visibility into application and infrastructure code risks before deployment, and giving security teams continuous monitoring of configurations, identities and workload behaviour.

The demo starts in the vulnerabilities view, where the tool ranks CVEs by checking whether vulnerable packages are actually running and exploitable in workloads. Container images that are active and exploitable rise to the top, while offline images can be deprioritised. An explorer view then maps relationships between risks on a virtual machine, showing internet exposure, critical vulnerabilities, misconfiguration and active threat alerts together to reveal possible exploitation paths and blast radius.

The presenter also shows a composite alert that combines several low-severity signals into one high-priority detection. In the example, a database server was compromised and used to install a crypto miner. An AI assistant is described as helping explain why an alert fired and how to respond. The demo closes with an identity view showing an account with far more permissions than it needs, illustrating how trimming unused privileges reduces the blast radius if credentials are stolen.

talks.title: The Latest FortiSASE Innovations at Accelerate 2025 | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Recaps FortiSASE's 2024 features and previews 2025 additions like a browser security add-on and Outpost.
talks.summary:
Filmed on the Tech Expo floor at Accelerate 2025, this short interview with Fortinet's senior director of product management, Claudio Salmin, looks back at FortiSASE's 2024 releases and forward to 2025. FortiSASE ships a new feature every month. He picked out three from last year. Agent-based ZTNA gives contractors without managed devices a portal where they see only the corporate applications they are allowed to reach. Remote browser isolation addresses risky or uncategorized websites. A thin-edge option steers traffic from small branches, with around 50 to 60 users each, into FortiSASE for security controls.

For 2025 he previewed an AI-related capability already shown at the expo, a browser security add-on that installs in the browser to protect users reaching web applications, due soon, and FortiSASE Outpost. Outpost lets an existing FortiGate act as a security point of presence that is managed directly from FortiSASE. He framed this as giving customers a choice of running security in the cloud or on premises.

The takeaway for existing FortiGate customers is that adopting FortiSASE is a transition rather than a replacement. They can keep their FortiGate devices and apply and control security from FortiSASE through a single management pane.

talks.title: What's New in FortiAppSec Cloud | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Explains Fortinet's SaaS application security service, bundling WAF, API protection, DDoS defense and bot mitigation without hardware.
talks.summary:
Idan Soen, VP of Product Management at Fortinet, introduces FortiAppSec Cloud as a SaaS application security service. He describes it as covering web and API security, DDoS protection and bot mitigation, alongside application availability and acceleration features such as enhanced routing, caching, compression and CDN-style content delivery. Because it is delivered as a service, nothing needs to be deployed on-premises as hardware or software, and protected applications can sit in a public cloud, on-premises, or in a hybrid environment.

On scope, he says the service is not limited to cloud-native applications. It can protect web or API applications, and both legacy and more modern applications fall within it. He also explains where the product came from: it brings together Fortinet's earlier standalone application security offerings, namely FortiWeb Cloud, FortiGSLB and FortiGuard advanced bot protection, into a single platform. He presents it as the next generation of those services.

For managed security providers, he outlines a partner route. MSSPs can resell licenses to their customers, manage the service on the customers' behalf, and onboard applications either directly or through the customer. The takeaway is an overview of the product's scope, deployment model and partner options rather than technical detail on how the protections work.

talks.title: Cuting Complexity with Fortinet Secure SD-Branch | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Cuting Complexity with Fortinet Secure SD-Branch | Accelerate25.

talks.title: Exploring Data Loss Prevention (DLP) | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Explains how data loss prevention differs from network security and outlines visibility, policy, and insider risk pillars.
talks.summary:
The segment opens with a distinction between data security and network security. Data security centers on reducing the risk that intellectual property and sensitive data are exposed in a customer environment, while network-facing controls in products such as FortiSASE, FortiGate, FortiOS, and FortiMail are described as an important part of overall data loss prevention and broader data security capabilities.

The discussion then walks through three pillars customers typically need in a data security program. First is visibility: understanding how information moves inside the organization, where it starts, where it goes, and where it might be exposed, with an upload to a service like Dropbox given as an example. Second is mitigation through policies that help employees make risk-informed choices when handling sensitive data, whether the business designs cars or operates as a bank. Third is deliberate data exfiltration and insider risk, including scenarios where someone leaving the organization tries to take data they feel they own.

The exchange closes with a direct yes-or-no question on whether artificial intelligence belongs in data security and data loss prevention; the answer given is yes. Practitioners hear a compact framing of how DLP sits beside network controls and which program areas—flow visibility, employee guidance, and insider-driven loss—to prioritize when building or evaluating capabilities.

talks.title: Unlock the Power of FortiAI | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Explains whether FortiAI is a built-in feature or a standalone product, and the operational value it is said to add.
talks.summary:
The interview opens with the question of whether FortiAI is a feature or a standalone product. The answer is that it is currently built into many Fortinet products, and that a new brand name for the technology was due to be announced shortly afterward. The speaker divides the offering into three parts. FortiAI Protect is aimed at organizations that want protection against unauthorized access attempts, which it can detect and prevent. FortiAI Assist is a virtual assistant built into numerous Fortinet offerings. A third element, also called FortiAI, is described as a secure artificial intelligence system.

On value, the speaker says generative AI reduces the manpower needed to process log data, which improves operational efficiency. The speaker also claims it raises the accuracy of tools used to identify threats. The discussion then turns to what the different AI offerings have in common. For FortiAI Assist, requests pass through a FortiAI proxy server in Fortinet's data center, and background processing runs on public cloud accounts that Fortinet owns. The speaker presents this as end-to-end protection of customer data during AI computation.

The segment closes by pointing viewers to fortinet.com for more information. It was streamed live from the Accelerate 25 technology expo. The main takeaway for a practitioner is that FortiAI is positioned both as features embedded in existing Fortinet products and as a branded product line. The claimed benefits are efficiency and detection accuracy, with a data path that Fortinet hosts and secures. The interview gives no technical detail on how these components work.

talks.title: The Future of FortiGate NGFWs | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Introduces the FortiGate 700G firewall, its 5-gigabit ports, and AI-driven threat detection features in the G series.
talks.summary:
This short interview from Fortinet's Accelerate 25 tech expo covers the latest FortiGate G series, which the host presents as an AI-powered firewall. The focus is the FortiGate 700G, a new model in the mid-range 40 series. Its standout feature is five multi-gigabit RJ45 ports that can run at 1, 2.5 or 5 gigabits, which can raise wireless bandwidth when the firewall connects many access points.

The guest positions the 700G between the 600F and the 900G. It offers about 26 gigabits of threat protection throughput and a similar interface, apart from the 5-gig ports. A new dedicated hardware module is said to make the appliance harder for attackers to target directly. On AI, the speaker points to upcoming software releases that add AI application visibility and a machine-learning-based IPS engine. Together, these show which AI applications users are running and help detect and block threats generated by AI.

The interview closes by noting that the G series currently includes the 700G and 900G, with more models planned. For practitioners, the main takeaways are the 700G's place as a mid-tier option and the description of AI-related visibility and detection features. The discussion stays at the product-positioning level and does not go into detailed technical specifications.

talks.title: FortiAnalyzer: The Power of a Single Data Lake & AI-Driven SOC | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in FortiAnalyzer: The Power of a Single Data Lake & AI-Driven SOC | Accelerate25.

talks.title: Stopping Breaches in Real Time with FortiEDR | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Explains why EDR matters at the endpoint, how it differs from signature-based protection, and how it extends into XDR.
talks.summary:
At Fortinet's Accelerate 25 Tech Expo, Shahir was interviewed about where endpoint detection and response (EDR) fits into an organisation's security setup. He argued that the endpoint is often the weakest link, because users open files and links that can carry threats such as ransomware, which makes EDR a critical product to run on every endpoint.

Asked whether EDR has made traditional endpoint protection obsolete, he said not entirely. Detection of known threats by signature still has a role, and EDR builds on it by recording the root cause, the chain of events and the behaviours a malicious action tries to carry out. That gives responders the identity of whoever acted and the ability to investigate back to the original event.

On product options, he described Fortinet offering EDR as a standalone product, and also inside a unified endpoint offering that combines access security and EDR in a single agent on the device. He added that the same capability extends to XDR, which brings detection and response together across the products in the Fortinet Security Fabric. The takeaway is that EDR should be a core endpoint control, and that its value depends on investigation depth as well as on catching known threats.

talks.title: Secure SD-WAN at Accelerate 2025 | Accelerate25
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Secure SD-WAN at Accelerate 2025 | Accelerate25.
talks.summary:
### Overview
Recorded live from the tech expo at Fortinet Accelerate 2025, this discussion explores the enduring relevance of SD-WAN amidst the industry shift toward SASE (Secure Access Service Edge). The speaker explains how Fortinet approaches SD-WAN not as a standalone, decoupled networking technology or an obsolete predecessor, but as an essential, core access foundation of SASE and secure networking.

### Key Topics
- **SD-WAN vs. SASE:** Addressing whether SD-WAN is at risk of becoming obsolete, the speaker clarifies that SD-WAN is more critical than ever because it provides the core access component connecting remote users and customer sites into a SASE architecture.
- **Secure SD-WAN vs. Standard SD-WAN:** Fortinet treats networking and security as inseparable. Rather than decoupling them, security is treated as a foundational baseline across all connectivity, whether site-to-site or site-to-SASE.
- **Market Validation:** Fortinet highlights being recognized as a Gartner Leader in the space for four consecutive years.

### Technical Details
Fortinet's SD-WAN architecture is characterized by key design principles:
- **Decentralization and Autonomous Operation:** Unlike solutions requiring continuous dependence on a remote centralized controller thousands of miles away, each SD-WAN device can function fully autonomously.
- **Flexible Security Consumption:** Customers can choose how they consume security—either locally on-box or cloud-delivered via FortiSASE.
- **Packaging and Management:** Secure SD-WAN functionality is fully included without licensing costs across all FortiGate appliances. In addition, centralized management via FortiManager includes the overlay orchestrator built-in at no extra charge.

### Takeaways
- SD-WAN remains a core access foundation for broader SASE architectures rather than a competing or obsolete technology.
- Secure SD-WAN provides autonomous edge survivability without continuous external controller dependencies.
- Fortinet includes full SD-WAN capabilities and overlay orchestration natively in FortiGate and FortiManager without separate licensing fees.

talks.title: Serial IO with FortiGate Rugged Firewalls | OT Security
talks.teaser: Shows how a FortiGate rugged firewall converts Modbus TCP commands into serial Modbus RTU for legacy PLCs.
talks.summary:
Industrial control systems often stay in service for a decade or more, so older serial-connected devices still need to work with modern Ethernet control networks. Matt Boolick, a technical marketing engineer at Fortinet, presents the industrial connectivity feature built into FortiGate rugged firewalls. It converts between a legacy serial protocol and its TCP/IP counterpart, with examples including IEC 101 to IEC 104, Modbus RTU to Modbus TCP, and serial TTL to IP raw socket. He contrasts this with dedicated serial gateways, which suit large serial systems, while the firewall suits a single device or one section being modernised.

The demo uses a Python application on a control station that sends a Modbus TCP command to the firewall's WAN interface. The firewall converts it to Modbus RTU, which triggers a serial-connected PLC to start filling a water tank, visible on an HMI screen. Setup requires enabling industrial connectivity on the ingress interface and then, from the CLI, which is reached through the GUI, three commands: enable industrial connectivity, set the translation type to Modbus, and select the serial interface. The default serial and Modbus settings worked for this setup.

In closing, Boolick notes that the firewall can also run raw socket transport, IEC 101 to 104 translation, or a changed Modbus unit ID when an environment requires it. The main takeaway is that existing serial devices can be bridged into a TCP/IP control network using a firewall already deployed, without adding separate serial hardware.

talks.title: OT Features of FortiAnalyzer | OT Security
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in OT Features of FortiAnalyzer | OT Security.

talks.title: OT Application Control with FortiGate Firewalls | OT Security
talks.teaser: Demonstrates FortiGate application controls and virtual patching for OT networks, including granular Modbus read filtering.
talks.summary:
The talk starts from the point where OT devices have already been discovered and security policies need to be enforced, whether the environment follows Purdue, NIST, IEC 62443 or NIS2. The demo runs in a simulated industrial environment with many devices from different vendors and generations, some carrying known vulnerabilities. Newly found assets appear in an OT view that places them in a Purdue-style layout based on device type and interfaces, and that layout can be rearranged to match a real environment.

Because some vulnerable devices cannot be patched right away in production, the presenter enables virtual patching. The default rule covers vulnerabilities of any severity, but it can be narrowed to specific severity levels or set to log only, so staff can act manually. The virtual patch profile is applied to firewall policies between the IT network and protected zones such as the control network. The security event logs then show a virtual patch already dropping only the traffic that matches an attack pattern against an Advantech device. The presenter notes over 1,300 virtual patching signatures and around 9,000 application signatures, more than 3,000 of them specific to OT, and shows how SIP can be filtered by message type.

To finish, the presenter creates an application rule. The default application sensor monitors signatures without acting on them, so an override is added for Modbus read. That override filters on unit and address values within chosen ranges, and it can be narrowed to a single unit and address. The rule is then attached to firewall policies. The closing argument is that one platform gives consistent control and management across IT and OT environments.

talks.title: OT Asset Identity with FortiGate Firewalls | OT Security
talks.teaser: Shows how a FortiGate firewall finds OT devices, adds vulnerability context, and places assets on the Purdue model.
talks.summary:
Unmanaged growth in OT networks often leaves unknown and outdated devices behind. This demo uses a FortiGate firewall and a FortiSwitch managed over FortiLink to build an asset inventory. The lab is a simulated OT network with VLANs spanning Purdue model levels and devices from many vendors. Detection starts on the operations and process VLANs, initially revealing only the network gear. It then finds a Windows device and an industrial device, using MAC addresses, ARP, DHCP and database lookups.

Thin details prompt the presenter to enable a default application control profile with OT signatures on a policy between monitoring and out-of-band management, and similar inspection between monitoring and control networks. SSL certificate inspection is turned on too. One device record then shows known vulnerabilities, including a command injection issue and a buffer error, each linked to its CVE. After a refresh, more assets appear, including Windows CE devices from Rockwell and another vendor and a RuggedCom device. The OT view places them on the Purdue model using device type and the interfaces where they were seen.

The takeaway is that one firewall can combine asset identity, vulnerability context and enforcement instead of relying on a separate discovery product. Placement in the Purdue view can be adjusted to match the real deployment. Virtual patching is left for a future video.

talks.title: Digital IO on FortiGate Rugged Firewalls | OT Security
talks.teaser: Shows how rugged firewall digital inputs and relay outputs link physical switches to automated Modbus policy changes.
talks.summary:
The talk explains digital IO, the physical input and relay output ports on FortiGate rugged firewalls and some rugged extender models. Inputs can sense an open or closed contact or a voltage difference, though they only register a state rather than measure voltage. The single relay output switches a common pin between normally open and normally closed contacts, with continuous current limited to 1 amp. The demo wiring includes an emergency stop button and red and green status lights on a 24 volt supply.

In normal operation, an LED application sends Modbus writes through the firewall to set the light strip color. Pressing the emergency button logs an input state change, which triggers a stitch running a CLI script. The script flips the relay so the status light turns red and switches the active policy to one that blocks red register writes with any value above zero. Blue and green writes still pass, so the red command times out in the application log. Releasing the switch restores the normal policy and the color cycle.

The presenter calls the example basic but argues that pairing physical sensing with protocol-level control is powerful for industrial networks. The setup covers input configuration, paired trigger stitches for the closed and open states, and documentation pointers for further digital IO settings. The takeaway is that firewall posture can change automatically in response to a physical condition.
