talks.title: FortiNAC Demo | Fortinet's Network Access Control Solution
talks.teaser: Demonstrates FortiNAC inventory, device profiling, VLAN enforcement and compliance checks, plus FortiGate tag sharing.
talks.summary:
The presenter defines network access control as technology that governs which users and devices, including IoT and OT equipment, can reach corporate infrastructure, based on authentication and endpoint posture. The demo covers the base features: visibility, guest access, endpoint compliance, secure BYOD and network segmentation. The platform can run as a hardware appliance, a virtual machine or a cloud instance.

The walkthrough starts with inventory. Administrators define sites as containers, seed discovery with IP lists or CDP crawling, and add SNMP and CLI credentials. The system then reads switch MAC and ARP tables to locate endpoints in real time, without requiring RADIUS. Devices are classified in several ways: through MDM connectors such as Intune, through captive-portal registration for guests, contractors and BYOD where sponsors approve requests by email, and through device profiling rules for agentless gear like cameras and phones. Profiling combines MAC filters, web page checks, DHCP fingerprinting, FortiGuard data and port or SSH and SNMP checks. Network access policies then map profiles to logical networks, which are bound to each switch's VLANs. Unknown devices move to the registration VLAN, failing devices to quarantine, and disabled devices to a dead-end VLAN.

The last part shows FortiGate integration, where classifications are shared as tags so firewall policies can match devices regardless of their IP address or interface. The main takeaway is that a complete inventory comes first, and policy should be built on abstract logical networks rather than per-switch VLAN definitions.

talks.title: FortiSIEM Unified Security Operations Analytics | FortiSIEM
talks.teaser: Shows FortiSIEM pulling Security Fabric device data through a REST API and flagging a firewall CPU incident.
talks.summary:
The demo presents FortiSIEM as a unified security operations analytics platform that connects to a Security Fabric through its REST API. The presenter starts from the fabric's physical topology view on a firewall, then creates a dedicated admin profile with permissions to query fabric data. A REST API administrator is mapped to that profile and issues an API token, which is entered in FortiSIEM as the device credential, using a custom port in place of the default 443.

With the credentials in place, a discovery run starting from one firewall finds the other firewalls attached behind it in the fabric. The discovered device then appears under the devices tab, where the summary shows host name, IP address, version and serial number, and where interfaces can be monitored and the configuration fetched. The relationship view shows the fabric hierarchy. The presenter then opens the security posture view, which gives the fabric's security rating and scores in one place, and generates a performance report covering average and maximum CPU utilization on the firewalls.

In the incident view, filtered by device, the presenter shows a performance incident on a firewall. The device was under a denial-of-service attack, CPU stayed above 90% for more than 10 minutes, and a rule raised that condition as an incident. The takeaway for analysts is to use per-device performance incidents to trace the root cause of high CPU events.

talks.title: FortiGuard Labs’ 2023 1H Threat Report | FortiGuardLIVE
talks.teaser: The session distills mid-year threat findings into ransomware trends, APT activity, and prioritization guidance for defenders.
talks.summary:
The conversation opens on FortiGuard Labs’ latest half-year threat landscape report and how the picture has shifted compared with prior years. On ransomware, volume has plateaued rather than climbing exponentially, but the speakers stress that risk has not fallen. Attacks are more targeted and patient, with criminal operators increasingly behaving like advanced persistent threat actors and focusing on high-value sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, and operational technology.

They highlight that a large share of tracked APT groups showed activity in the reporting period, tying cyber operations to ongoing geopolitical tension and closer cooperation between nation-state and criminal ecosystems. For defense, they describe “threat-informed defense” ideas from the report, including the Red Zone: correlating endpoint vulnerability exposure with intrusion-prevention detections so leaders see which issues are both open and under attack—often a small fraction of the full CVE corpus. They also explain tying outbreak alerts to EPSS, using the MOVEit case as an example of scoring exploitation likelihood before mass in-the-wild abuse.

The discussion closes on attack-sighting data mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, noting that a majority of techniques appear in real activity and urging security operations to feed those observations into red-team testing and blue-team detection. The overall message is that predictive and correlated data can help defenders focus patching and response instead of drowning in raw vulnerability counts.

talks.title: Gaining Management Efficiency With Fortinet | Customer Stories
talks.teaser: Shows how a hotel group with thousands of properties used converged networking and security to replace fragmented per-site management.
talks.summary:
Melvin, a hotel security compliance director at IHG, describes the scale of the company's footprint: about 6,195 hotels now, up from roughly 2,000 when he started, with around 300,000 employees across three regions. Each region runs its own operations, while global security policies and technology standards are set centrally. Guests are on property constantly, which makes the threat surface large, and each hotel depends on a wide ecosystem of systems such as parking, keycard and check-in, run by different vendors and owners.

The main problem he describes is management. Every property effectively operates as its own data center, and the older architecture gives no centralized control, so it is hard to see what is happening across the estate from one place. Converging networking and security gives him a higher-level picture of security, infrastructure and bandwidth at each property. He argues that convergence will become the direction of the industry and that leadership will see its business value as it spreads.

He closes with a view on vendors and partners. Vendors drive scope and service levels, while partners want to understand the business and its pain points so both sides can grow together. The accompanying description frames the deployment as using the Fortinet Security Fabric and Secure SD-WAN to converge networking and security. The takeaway is that centralized visibility and a true partner relationship matter as much as the technology itself.

talks.title: Rethinking Networking and Security For The Campus And Branch With Fortinet | Packet Pushers Podcast
talks.teaser: Explores how Fortinet pitches converged campus, branch, IoT and operations tooling as a single platform for networking and security.
talks.summary:
This sponsored Packet Pushers podcast features two Fortinet executives discussing how the vendor's portfolio now spans firewalls, switching, wireless, WAN and SASE rather than firewalls alone. The guests argue that running one operating system across products and managing them from one console avoids the integration work that comes with mixing vendors.

A central section covers campus and branch networks. For smart-building and IoT or OT devices, the speakers describe automatic device identification and segmentation, plus virtual patching that applies network-level mitigations to devices that cannot be updated. For branches, they point to unmanaged equipment and shadow IT as visibility problems, and to central management that applies the same policy at every site. Micro branches with one or a few users can be covered by inspection on access points or a SASE client on the device.

The final part addresses operations. The guests claim that correlating telemetry from firewalls, access points and switches in one platform shortens root cause analysis, moving from separate vendor systems to a single view. They also mention a managed SOC service to offset the skills shortage and a flexible consumption licensing program. The practical takeaway is that fewer, consistently integrated tools reduce daily workload, though much of the discussion is vendor positioning rather than independent evaluation.

talks.title: The Role of Transparency in Cybersecurity | 2023 Security Summit at the Fortinet Championship
talks.teaser: Panelists argue that openly disclosing vulnerabilities and sharing information builds the trust needed for stronger security.
talks.summary:
A panel at a Fortinet security summit examines why transparency matters for trust in the products organizations rely on. Former Department of Homeland Security under secretary Suzanne Spalding frames the idea as learning to fight in daylight, arguing that secrets have a short shelf life and that organizations should plan for adversaries eventually getting in. She links this to the post-9/11 move from need-to-know to need-to-share, and warns that over-classification and reluctance to disclose leave defenders weaker.

Carl Windsor, Fortinet's product CSO, explains that the company publishes advisories for every vulnerability, whether it was found internally or reported externally. He suggests buyers judge vendors by reading public advisories and release notes, noting that many bugs with few vulnerabilities can signal limited scrutiny. Spalding adds that mandatory incident reporting, standard disclosure timelines and common scoring such as CVSS would put everyone on equal footing.

The discussion closes on secure-by-default and secure-by-design goals. Windsor outlines Fortinet's changes, including static analysis and vulnerability scanning on every build, threat modeling, retiring weaker encryption settings, and labelling maturity releases with optional scheduled upgrades. Spalding says shifting responsibility to manufacturers and rewarding security in the market will be needed. The takeaway is to expect vulnerabilities, favor vendors that disclose openly and patch quickly, and prefer products that are safe out of the box.

talks.title: Series 3 of 3: Security Fabric Integration | Security Fabric
talks.teaser: Shows how FortiGate, FortiWeb and FortiADC combine with other Fortinet products into a full application security architecture.
talks.summary:
This final part of a three-video series on application security with Fortinet products presents a complete reference topology. It builds on earlier material about choosing between FortiADC and FortiWeb and about reference architectures, placing FortiGate as the firewall foundation and layering the wider portfolio around it. The design is organized into client access, operations, application and enhancement segments.

On the access side, FortiClient serves as the endpoint agent and FortiRecon provides digital risk protection, covering external attack surface management, brand protection and dark web monitoring. The operations tier uses FortiManager and FortiADC Manager to oversee deployed devices, FortiAnalyzer for logs and reporting, FortiMonitor for digital experience monitoring and FortiDeceptor for deception. The application tier adds FortiDevSec for continuous testing in CI/CD pipelines and FortiAuthenticator for identity and access management that integrates with LDAP or Active Directory. Among the enhancers, FortiSandbox isolates suspicious files and URLs in a virtual environment, and FortiWeb Cloud threat analytics groups large volumes of alerts into incidents.

The guidance is to always deploy FortiGate, place FortiDDoS in front of it when needed, position load balancers behind the firewall, and run devices in high availability pairs. Decrypting SSL and TLS at the load balancing tier gives inspection visibility into encrypted traffic. The video also covers FortiGSLB for DNS-based routing and a simplified cloud deployment built on FortiGate VM and FortiWeb Cloud. The main takeaway is that combining these products protects every segment while keeping applications available under load.

talks.title: FortiWeb Bot Protection Demo | Web Application Firewall
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of FortiWeb Bot Protection Demo | Web Application Firewall.
talks.summary:
### Overview
This demonstration video highlights FortiWeb's bot defense and bot mitigation capabilities, specifically focusing on safeguarding e-commerce websites against transaction fraud executed by retail bots.

### Key Topics
- **Major Web Application Use Cases**: FortiWeb covers five primary use cases: web application security, bot defense, regulatory compliance, protecting internet APIs, and SOC operations.
- **Retail Bot Threats**: Attackers deploy retail bots to automate account registration, account login, profile submission, adding items to shopping carts, and final checkout. The malicious goal behind these automated retail bots is often profiting by reselling products while preventing legitimate shoppers from purchasing goods.
- **FortiWeb Bot Mitigation**: Configuring and enabling bot defense stops automated purchase workflows and blocks bot transactions.

### Technical Details
- **Biometric-Based Detection**: FortiWeb checks client events, such as touchscreen, mouse, and keyboard interactions, to distinguish whether an incoming web request originates from a human or an automated bot.
- **Policy Configuration**: To implement bot mitigation, the biometric-based detection is enabled, added into a bot mitigation policy, and then associated with the web protection profile inside the server policy.
- **Attack Blocking and Verification**: When the retail bot attempts the automated checkout sequence after protection is enabled, FortiWeb successfully blocks the purchase attempt, which can be verified and reviewed directly within FortiWeb's attack logs.
- **Detection Techniques**: In addition to biometrics, FortiWeb defends against automated threats using IP reputation, signatures, traffic thresholds, analysis of keyboard and mouse interactions, bot deception, and machine learning.

### Takeaways
Automated retail bots can rapidly disrupt commerce by monopolizing inventory and executing fraudulent transactions. FortiWeb effectively mitigates bot-driven attacks by layering multiple detection techniques—ranging from biometric and behavioral tracking to signatures and machine learning—enabling administrators to monitor threats via attack logs and preserve service availability for legitimate users.

talks.title: FortiGate Azure vWAN SD-WAN | FortiGate
talks.teaser: Shows how to deploy FortiGate firewalls as SD-WAN hubs in Azure Virtual WAN and test branch access to Azure resources.
talks.summary:
The talk looks at how branch offices and endpoints can reach virtual networks in Azure through Azure Virtual WAN, where virtual hubs are interconnected to form a global transit backbone. Microsoft lets third-party security vendors run network virtual appliances inside a virtual WAN hub, and this demonstration deploys FortiGate next-generation firewall instances there as SD-WAN hubs. Once running, the hub appliances can inspect north-south, east-west and internet-bound traffic.

The walkthrough starts in the Azure portal, where a virtual WAN and a hub are created and a virtual network holding protected resources is connected to that hub. A FortiGate appliance is then deployed from the Azure Marketplace into the same region, with the BGP ASN noted so it matches the hub configuration. Routing intent is set so private and internet-bound traffic passes through the appliance. Each appliance is authorized in FortiManager, given static routes toward the hub router and the Azure load balancer probe address, and paired in a high-availability setup with session synchronization for asymmetric traffic. BGP peering with the Azure hub is then established.

On the FortiManager side, an SD-WAN overlay template is built with dual hubs and ADVPN enabled, using the same ASN as the appliances. Branch devices receive metadata values and CLI templates for DHCP gateway assignment, and their SD-WAN zone and a firewall rule for branch-to-Azure traffic are configured before policy packages are installed. The closing test uses a Windows 10 client in a branch subnet to reach a protected resource in Azure over the overlay, and the connection succeeds. The main takeaway is that ASN matching, routing and probe handling in the hub are what make the setup work, and templates make adding branches repeatable.

talks.title: SD-WAN Based Traffic Steering at FortiSASE PoP | Network Security
talks.teaser: Demonstrates SD-WAN path steering for private application traffic in a FortiSASE PoP, with failover to a backup data center.
talks.summary:
The talk walks through a cloud-delivered secure private access use case in FortiSASE, where SD-WAN steers traffic across several points of presence and two data centers. Each PoP acts as a spoke connected to SD-WAN hubs in AWS, with a primary and a backup data center. The presenter shows the cloud console settings: a BGP router ID, subnet, autonomous system number, and a path selection criterion based on link quality or BGP MED value, plus an IP address used to monitor service connections. The platform builds the IPsec tunnels, BGP and SD-WAN rules automatically, and manual priority per service connection is also supported.

The demo uses an endpoint connected to the San Jose PoP. Link quality checks show the primary data center preferred because of lower latency and jitter. A web server on a private AWS subnet is first reached from the Northern California region. The presenter then introduces latency and packet loss on that server with an emulator. After a browser refresh, the session moves to a web server instance in the Northern Virginia region. Link statistics in the console show higher latency and loss on the primary path than on the backup, which justifies the steering decision.

To close, the talk notes that the PoPs provide full mesh connectivity through auto-discovery VPN, removing the need for dedicated IPsec tunnels between sites. The takeaway for practitioners is that SD-WAN and ADVPN support at each PoP can simplify network architecture and operations for private application access.

talks.title: Welcome to FortiGate Cloud | Fortinet
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Welcome to FortiGate Cloud | Fortinet.
talks.summary:
### Overview
Cyber attacks present a significant risk not only to large enterprises but also to smaller organizations. Threats like ransomware, wipers, and Trojans allow threat actors to establish footholds and disrupt business operations. For organizations operating with limited budgets and cybersecurity expertise, deploying, analyzing, and managing network security solutions efficiently can be a challenge. Fortinet positions FortiGate Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) and FortiGate Cloud as solutions designed to safeguard mission-critical networks without introducing additional complexity or expense.

### Key Topics
FortiGate Cloud is a cloud-based service delivering centralized management, security analytics, and reporting for FortiGate firewalls and connected network infrastructure. Key focus areas covered in the talk include:
- Centralized, simplified management across firewalls and connected downstream equipment.
- Zero-touch provisioning for accelerated initial deployment and setup.
- Real-time and historical network visibility, logging, and security reporting.
- Tier differences between free and paid subscription models.

### Technical Details
- **Device Management & Zero-Touch Provisioning:** FortiGate Cloud enables centralized management for FortiGate firewalls as well as downstream connected Fortinet devices, including FortiAP, FortiSwitch, and FortiExtender. Administrators can access devices remotely via the cloud without needing to recall specific IP addresses or device credentials. Supported administrative actions include adjusting network configurations, modifying security policies and profiles, running custom scripts, scheduling cloud backups, and executing software upgrades across single or multiple FortiGate devices simultaneously.
- **Traffic Analytics and Logging:** The platform provides real-time and historical visibility into system events, applications, web traffic, and security threats. System and security events are logged in the cloud, permitting long-term log retrieval.
- **Reporting Capabilities:** FortiGate Cloud supports on-demand and scheduled reports to uncover risk trends, validate security enhancements, and satisfy reporting mandates. Available formats include web activity reports, application usage reports, and Cyber Threat Assessment Reports.
- **Sandbox Inspection:** An add-on license is available to provide Cloud Sandbox services for analyzing and inspecting files against zero-day malware.
- **Subscription Comparison:**
  - *Free Tier:* Includes standard cloud access to FortiGate and downstream devices, but limits cloud log retention to 7 days and supports only a single report.
  - *Paid Tier:* Delivers unrestricted configuration management for FortiGate and downstream connected devices, alongside up to one full year of cloud retention for Enterprise-grade security analytics and reporting logs.

### Takeaways
FortiGate Cloud enables organizations with constrained IT and security resources to streamline operations and decrease cyber risks. Centralizing policy control, simplifying provisioning, and leveraging extended reporting and cloud sandbox capabilities allows teams to detect threats earlier and maintain comprehensive visibility across their network fabric.

talks.title: FortiGuard AI-Driven Content Security | Product Demo
talks.teaser: Shows FortiGate blocking test malware, sanitizing active PDF content and stopping credit card data leaks through live demos.
talks.summary:
This video is a product demonstration of the content security services in the FortiGate advanced threat protection bundle, covering antivirus, content disarm and reconstruction, virus outbreak prevention and data leak prevention. The presenter runs each test from a Windows host behind a FortiGate. Sandboxing is set aside for a separate video.

The antivirus demo uses the standard EICAR test file in its plain form, with a renamed extension, and inside zip archives nested one and two levels deep. Each download is blocked, and the block page names the virus and links to more information. The antivirus profile is applied to an outbound firewall policy along with SSL deep inspection, and the log entry records the profile and policy used. For content disarm and reconstruction, a PDF containing a JavaScript clock is downloaded and arrives with a cover sheet, its active content removed while the text stays readable. The presenter notes this mode requires proxy-mode inspection. Virus outbreak prevention blocks a file by querying the vendor's global threat intelligence in real time, intended to cover the gap between signature updates.

Data leak prevention is tested by pasting a spreadsheet of fictional credit card numbers into a website and attempting an HTTPS post, which is blocked and logged. The setup needs three parts: a dictionary defining the sensitive data, a sensor that uses it, and rules that set the protocols and whether messages or files are scanned. The takeaway is that these controls are attached to firewall policies and their events are reviewed in the security event logs.

talks.title: SD-Campus Architecture | Secure Networking
talks.teaser: Shows how a headquarters campus network secures wireless, switches and IoT devices with firewalls, access control and zero trust.
talks.summary:
The talk walks through the security architecture of Fortinet's new headquarters campus, a building designed as a zero-carbon-emission site that already operates as carbon neutral. Its automated lighting, window shades and HVAC systems, along with a growing number of headless IoT and OT devices, bring the kinds of problems industrial environments have dealt with for years. The speaker argues that a modern campus needs a security architecture built from the ground up.

Scale is the first concern: nearly 150,000 square feet of space and hundreds of employees who need secure connectivity every day. Over 200 access points across the two-building campus serve both staff and automated control devices, and around 200 switches connect voice, camera and other critical systems. The FortiGate next-generation firewall controls and secures these network components, extending protection out to devices as they join, with built-in network access control placing each device into the correct security context. Secure SD-WAN improves application access regardless of location, and FortiGuard services add URL and DNS filtering, application control, inline sandboxing and device security for IoT and OT systems.

To close, the talk covers Universal ZTNA, which gives employees consistent access from anywhere and checks every user and device before granting access to an application, reducing the attack surface. The takeaway is that a campus with many unmanaged devices benefits from per-device context and verification rather than trusting the network perimeter.

talks.title: Global 2023 State of Operational Technology and Cybersecurity Report | FortinetLIVE
talks.teaser: Field CISOs unpack a 2023 survey on OT security posture, intrusions, and threat intelligence use in industrial environments.
talks.summary:
This episode of Fortinet Live has Jim Richburg, Fortinet's field CISO for the public sector, talking with colleague Willie Nelson about the 2023 State of Operational Technology and Cybersecurity Report. They note that OT remains a frequent target, that malware and phishing are still the most commonly reported incident types, and that fewer respondents now rate their OT posture as highly mature. Nearly 80 percent of respondents reported large fleets of IP-enabled OT devices, and sprawling security tools make consistent policy enforcement difficult.

The speakers dig into several surprises. Responsibility for OT security is moving toward chief security officers, with the share of organizations placing it there rising sharply to 95 percent. They also discuss breach reporting, where fewer incidents hit only OT while more affected IT or both, which they describe as shared pain that boards now ask about. Use of cyber threat intelligence dipped, which Nelson attributes to OT teams struggling to turn intelligence into action. Role-based access control was measured for the first time, with over half of organizations using it, and they expect that number to climb.

For practitioners, the guidance starts with knowing which assets are critical and being honest in self-assessments, since compliance can create a false sense of posture. Recommended steps include consolidating vendors to reduce complexity, using network access control to spot rogue devices, treating zero trust as a long journey, and running user awareness training. The closing message is to plan for failure, build response playbooks, and rely on classic risk management rather than reinventing it.

talks.teaser: A partner view delivers Engage specializations, compliance pressure, and converged networking as prerequisites for security outcomes.
talks.summary:
The session opens with Fortinet and North Atlantic Networks (NAN) framing a partner conversation around Engage program specializations, including SD-WAN, LAN edge, SD branch, and data center focus areas. Burke Anderson describes NAN’s evolution from dial-up-era origins toward managed security services built around Fortinet engineering certifications and a narrowing security practice.

He explains why the firm invested in Fortinet credentials, values engineer-to-engineer support, and uses the broad product stack for digital transformation engagements. Customer demand centers on talent shortages, compliance frameworks such as CMMC, and rebuilds after breaches, with NAN positioning deployments as multi-year journeys rather than quick firewall installs.

Anderson stresses convergence between networking and security: firewalls, switches, access points, cloud links, and carrier experience must align before security outcomes work. He advises new partners to pursue certifications, specialize where connectivity matters, and lean on vendor training and sales support.

talks.title: Q2 Update on Recent Threat Trends | FortiGuardLIVE
talks.teaser: Surveys deep fake voice and video risks for phishing and fraud, and why spotting synthesized media at scale still outpaces most defenses.
talks.summary:
The episode frames deep fakes as a narrow branch of machine learning used to make faces and voices appear to say scripted content. One presenter walks through how models learn accents, pauses, expressions, and mannerisms from large public audio and video sets, and how creators already use the same tooling for training videos without live camera time.

The conversation centers on abuse: voice clones from short recordings or casual calls, celebrity and executive impersonation, and multi-step scams that stack phishing email, vishing, and fake video meetings on top of familiar business email compromise playbooks. Commodity sites and open models have pushed costs down and put generation within reach of commodity hardware, with paid deep-fake services already circulating.

Detection is portrayed as immature compared with email or endpoint controls. Fingerprints in some public generators may help in theory, but continuous inspection of RTP voice and encrypted video traffic raises operational cost. Examples cited include election influence, a social-media deep fake image tied to a brief market move, and the need for legal responses that do not map cleanly to global attackers.

talks.title: Military Makeover: Fortinet Offers Veterans Careers in Cybersecurity | Fortinet Veterans Program
talks.teaser: A Fortinet program shows how veterans can move into cybersecurity careers through training, mentoring and job placement.
talks.summary:
Fortinet's veterans program recruits former service members and their spouses into cybersecurity roles. The talk opens with the company's commitment to training one million people by 2026, then several veterans describe their own paths out of the military. One started as a security policeman and later cross-trained into computer systems work, while another spent four years as a Marine Corps administrative clerk before switching to a computer systems job and spending 16 years in computing and cybersecurity.

The middle of the talk explains the field in plain terms. Every connected device a person owns widens an organization's attack surface, and defenders' job is to protect networks and operations so companies and governments can recover services quickly after an attack. The presenters note that the sensitive data at stake depends on the industry, from operational technology in critical infrastructure to patient records in healthcare, and that adversaries look to profit from all of it.

The closing section covers the program itself. Fortinet works with partner organizations to help veterans prepare resumes and find mentors, trains them in security skills, and commits to placing those who are not hired internally with a partner employer. Speakers stress that most of their job leads came through networking rather than online applications, and that military discipline, integrity and problem-solving carry over well into civilian roles.

talks.title: FortiGuard AI-Driven Web Security: Video Filtering | FortiGuard Security Services
talks.teaser: Shows how FortiGuard video filtering applies category and channel rules to YouTube through YouTube's APIs.
talks.summary:
This is the third video in a FortiGuard series on AI-driven web security, and it focuses on video filtering for YouTube. The presenter explains that the service applies the same granular controls used for other web traffic to YouTube, including channel-level rules beyond broad categories, by working through YouTube's programming interfaces. The example is an organization that wants staff to watch only knowledge-based videos without hurting productivity, while still keeping some research content available.

The demonstration starts with a video filter profile that blocks every video category except knowledge. That profile is attached to a firewall policy alongside the default application control and SSL deep inspection profiles. A music video is shown being blocked with its category displayed, while a Microsoft Excel tutorial in the knowledge category keeps playing. The web filtering logs then record the event type, video category and firewall policy, and tie each attempt to a specific video ID so the blocked videos can be matched to their categories.

In the second scenario, every category is blocked but the official Fortinet channel is added to a channel override list. Only videos from that channel play, while other videos are stopped, and the logs show each blocked entry under its own category. The practical takeaway is that channel-level overrides let administrators permit specific trusted sources on YouTube while still blocking the rest of the platform.

talks.title: FortiGate-VM: GCP Organization Restrictions | Cloud Security
talks.teaser: Shows how a FortiGate-VM egress proxy can restrict managed devices to approved Google Cloud organizations.
talks.summary:
The talk explains how identity and access management in Google Cloud can be paired with an egress proxy to keep employees on managed devices from reaching resources outside approved organizations. The stated goal is to reduce data exfiltration through phishing or insider activity. Traffic from a managed device passes through an egress proxy that adds an organization restriction header to each request, and Google Cloud inspects that header and allows or blocks the request based on the organization being accessed.

The demo walks through configuring a FortiGate-VM as an explicit web proxy. The browser on the managed device points at the FortiGate's public address, with a listening interface and HTTP port set and a proxy policy created for the outgoing interface and destination addresses. A web proxy profile, which can only be set from the CLI, holds the Google Cloud organization ID, and a set content command places that ID into the headers. The ID is looked up with gcloud by listing the project's ancestors.

The result is shown in two checks. Access to a resource in the non-authorized organization is denied in the browser, while the authorized organization's resource loads. A packet sniffer on port 8080 lets the viewer watch the proxied requests pass through the FortiGate. The takeaway is that proxy administrators and Google Cloud administrators must coordinate so each organization is restricted correctly.

talks.title: Conquering the Tyranny of Distance While Halving Annual Networking Costs | Customer Stories
talks.teaser: A customer story covers halving WAN spend with SD-WAN, site firewalls, and IT-OT separation at remote freight yards.
talks.summary:
Pacific National, Australia’s largest freight railroad, outlines why always-on systems and strong cyber defenses matter across roughly eighty locations serving heavy intermodal and bulk freight. Legacy WAN design was costly, offered weak edge security, and forced internet traffic through centralized data centers—painful for remote yards with poor fiber options.

The organization moved to a software-defined WAN built around Fortinet firewalls, switches, and wireless at each site, plus refreshed data-center networking, with tight on-site collaboration between vendor and internal teams. Reported outcomes include about a fifty-percent reduction in overall network spend, Wi-Fi at every site, Telstra or Optus 4G failover when links fail, and per-site bandwidth rising from roughly twenty megabits toward four hundred megabits through active use of bundled paths.

Local internet breakout, centralized management of a large distributed firewall fleet, and clearer separation between IT and OT networks are framed as core security wins, alongside web application firewall and related edge controls. The closing message is a more reliable, agile, and cheaper wide-area network that staff—including drivers updating phones and using FaceTime—can rely on daily.

talks.title: FortiGuard AI-Driven Web Security: Secure DNS Filtering | FortiGuard Security Services
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding FortiGuard AI-Driven Web Security: Secure DNS Filtering | FortiGuard Security Services.
talks.summary:
FortiGuard Secure DNS Filtering

Overview
This presentation is the second video in a FortiGuard AI-driven web security series, focusing on DNS filtering as a key component of Fortinet's web security service. DNS filtering blocks entire domains and all associated URLs, whereas web filtering blocks specific web pages. The web security subscription comprises web and content filtering, secure DNS, and video filtering.

Key Capabilities and Threats Addressed
FortiGuard Secure DNS protects against sophisticated DNS-based threats including DNS tunneling, command-and-control (C&C) server identification, and domain generation algorithms. The service provides full visibility into DNS traffic and can block higher-risk domains including malicious domains, newly registered domains, and parked domains. Users can configure block settings at the DNS level based on various predefined categories.

Technical Implementation
FortiGate Next Generation Firewall blocks connections at both DNS and connection levels for comprehensive protection. Starting with FortiOS 7.0, FortiGate can inspect encrypted DNS traffic: DNS over TLS (using TCP port 853) and DNS over HTTPS (using TCP port 443). Configuration is performed through the DNS filter security profile in the FortiGate GUI. Security events and DNS query logs provide visibility into blocked requests and domain categorization.

Practical Use Cases
The presentation demonstrates two scenarios: First, a K-8 school environment using DNS filtering for compliance with child protection regulations by blocking categories of inappropriate content. Configuration involves creating a named DNS profile with selected blocked categories and applying it to firewall policies. Second, blocking botnet and C&C domains, with successful blocks visible in DNS query logs.

Pre-configured Filters
Desktop FortiGate models (such as the FortiGate 40F) include pre-configured filters resembling movie ratings: G (all ages, strictest), PG-13 (more lenient), and R (most lenient), with custom filter options. These simplify profile creation for environments with child and teenage users.

Key Differentiation
Fortinet includes DNS protection as part of the web security subscription, whereas some competitors offer DNS protection as a separate service.

talks.title: Credential Phishing Prevention | FortiGuard's AI Powered Security
talks.teaser: Shows how FortiGate's credential phishing prevention blocks corporate logins typed into external websites.
talks.summary:
The talk opens with the case for focusing on phishing. The presenter cites the FBI's 2022 Internet Crime Report, where phishing was the most common crime type in the United States, with reported growth of more than 1,100 percent from 2018 to its 2021 peak. The feature covered is credential phishing prevention, part of FortiGuard's web filtering service on FortiGate firewalls.

The mechanism works by inspecting submissions to external sites for corporate credentials and comparing them against sensitive credentials held in the corporate domain controller. Depending on the configured anti-phishing rules, the firewall either blocks the URL or alerts the user when a match occurs. In a live demo, a domain user's username and password typed into a Facebook login page were blocked, and the user saw a web filter violation page explaining that internal credentials had been submitted to an external site. A made-up username and password passed through, as expected, since they do not match a domain account.

The presenter then checked the web filtering logs under the security events page, where the Facebook attempt appeared with an entry showing that the request contained known credentials. Finally, the web filter profile was shown applied to an outbound firewall policy. For administrators, the takeaway is that the control catches reused corporate passwords on outside sites, but it only takes effect once the profile is attached to the outbound rule.

talks.title: The Convergence of Networking and Security | Accelerate 2023
talks.teaser: Argues that secure networking is overtaking traditional networking and that platform consolidation is reshaping vendors.
talks.summary:
The keynote opens with the claim that secure networking, which inspects traffic by application, user and device rather than only routing it, will outgrow traditional networking over the next decade. The speaker traces this to the original internet design, which assumed every connection shared one trust level. He argues that cloud, mobile and IoT connections still rely on the same network protocols and do not address content or application context, so inline security keeps gaining importance.

The middle of the talk turns to consolidation. The speaker contrasts vendors that grow mainly through acquisition with a single-platform approach built on in-house development. He says single-function security products tend to disappear once larger platforms absorb their features, and that running many separate inline devices is costly, slow and hard to manage. The argument then covers a product fabric running one operating system, custom ASICs that offload security functions from the CPU, and a broad partner ecosystem.

The closing section addresses service providers, arguing that security delivered as a service must be scalable, reliable and deployable across on-premises, cloud and remote environments on a shared platform. The speaker presents performance and energy comparisons for a new hardware generation as evidence for his thesis. The takeaway for practitioners is that they should expect fewer, more integrated platforms in place of many point products.

talks.title: Accelerate 2023 Ultimate Fabric Challenge Winners | FortinetLIVE
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning Accelerate 2023 Ultimate Fabric Challenge Winners | FortinetLIVE.
talks.summary:
Overview
This FortinetLIVE segment features interviews with the three top winners of the 2023 Ultimate Fabric Challenge (UFC) Global Championship, held at Accelerate 2023. The UFC is a skills-based competition where participants competed in regional rounds at partner expert summits throughout 2022 before advancing to the global championship.

The Winners
Andrea Fidelity, a solution architect, won first place in the UFC Global Championship. Sarah Ryba, a network engineer at Liquid Networks in San Antonio, Texas, placed second. Marvin Carrasco, a business development manager, placed third.

Preparation Strategies
All three winners emphasized the importance of hands-on experience with FortiGate devices and leveraging FortiNet's available resources. Andrea highlighted real-life configuration experience as essential, supplemented by the FortiNet Training Institute for learning new products and solutions. Sarah combined extensive experience configuring the FortiNet fabric suite and security fabric with multiple NSC (Fortinet Certified Associate) certifications. She also utilized FortiNet admin guides, product demos, and developer network resources. Marvin similarly relied on varied configuration experience across FortiNet solutions and preparation for NSC exams.

Role of NSC Training in Career Development
All three stressed how NSC training and certifications accelerated their careers. Andrea noted it provided foundational cybersecurity knowledge early in her career and enabled her to master new FortiNet security products. Sarah emphasized that Fortinet certifications helped her develop well-rounded technical knowledge, allowing her to better serve customers and suggest relevant FortiNet features. Marvin praised the NSC program as comprehensive and well-designed, covering cybersecurity fundamentals, FortiNet solutions, tools, scripting languages, and real-world integration scenarios.

Advice for Future Competitors
The winners unanimously recommended three key points: prepare thoroughly using FortiNet resources, enjoy the competition, and focus on confidence and speed during execution. They noted that all competitors have the capability to complete objectives given available resources—the differentiator is speed and self-assurance. Sarah specifically highlighted that having fun reduces anxiety and improves performance. Marvin encouraged exploring the full FortiNet product portfolio beyond core certifications.

talks.title: Firewalls Explained | Fortinet Channel Sync
talks.teaser: A chronological tour shows how packet filters grew into next-generation firewalls with deep inspection and micro-segmentation.
talks.summary:
The presentation opens by tying average breach recovery costs to the role of firewalls as a network’s first defensive layer, then walks through how the technology matured in distinct generations.

Early packet filters from 1989 allowed or denied traffic using headers—source, destination, protocol, and port—via access control lists, but stateless rules could not follow sessions and were easy to abuse. Stateful firewalls added connection tracking; application-layer devices could distinguish legitimate web traffic from unwanted uses of the same protocol and port. Next-generation designs combine those capabilities with deep packet inspection of payloads, optional sandbox analysis for suspicious content, and segmentation—including virtual rules in cloud environments—to limit lateral movement. The narrative also notes consolidation of formerly standalone functions such as intrusion prevention and related filtering.

The closing segment addresses endpoint and home use: most desktops and laptops ship with host firewalls, while antivirus and VPN extend protection to portable gear. Routers often cover basic needs, but IoT and similar devices without full operating systems may still require dedicated perimeter or consumer firewall options.

talks.title: OT Security Shop Talk: Adopting New Technologies and The Cloud | Operational Technology
talks.teaser: Discusses how industrial operators are adopting cloud, AI and IIoT devices, and the security concerns that follow.
talks.summary:
The discussion opens with the pressure facing industrial operators, many of whose security postures rest on technology several generations old. As they try to keep pace, they are looking at artificial intelligence and machine learning fed by data from deep within operational technology networks, along with more effective use of cloud services such as AWS Greengrass. The speakers also point to industrial internet of things devices, which are often deployed in far riskier ways than traditional OT equipment, changing what an OT environment looks like.

The conversation then turns to the long-standing resistance to cloud in OT. One speaker recalls that raising cloud in an OT meeting used to draw hostility. They note that IT went through the same objections years ago, when lines of business insisted they would never move, and that most of those organizations now run in the cloud. The panel sees OT following a similar path, especially where moving workloads offers a way to optimize operations or save money.

The main takeaway is that OT teams should expect cloud, AI and IIoT to reach their environments whether or not they feel ready. Security planning needs to account for that shift, including the older equipment already in place and the new devices that will connect to it.

talks.title: Tech Bytes: Protecting Any Edge at Any Scale | Packet Pushers
talks.teaser: Hosts survey firewall chassis news, NetBox funding, IT executive fines, cloud spending claims, juice-jacking warnings, and chip deals.
talks.summary:
The episode opens with product and funding news, including Fortinet’s large FortiGate 7081 chassis firewall with high port counts, ASIC-offloaded inspection, and campus-scale stacking, plus NetBox Labs’ $20 million Series A to grow its open-source network source-of-truth platform.

Discussion turns to accountability when major outages hit banks and consumer platforms, contrasting UK regulator fines on a former bank CIO with Tencent leadership changes after WeChat and QQ downtime. The hosts then unpack Andy Jassy’s shareholder letter on slowing AWS growth, elastic cloud costs, and the claim that roughly ninety percent of global IT spend remains on premises.

Later segments reassess public juice-jacking warnings against sparse real-world evidence, note steep Q1 2023 PC shipment declines, Intel Foundry’s ARM manufacturing pact, Broadcom–VMware regulatory friction, and Microsoft’s plan to remap Print Screen in Windows 11 before sign-off.

talks.title: Enterprise-Class Protection Against Internet-Borne Threats | FortiProxy
talks.teaser: Shows FortiProxy explicit-proxy flow, profiles, and live enforcement for filtering, antivirus, DLP, and AI image controls.
talks.summary:
The session introduces FortiProxy as Fortinet’s secure web gateway for internet-borne threats, combining web and DNS filtering, data loss prevention, antivirus, intrusion prevention, browser isolation, and related controls. It explains explicit-proxy packet flow: HTTPS traffic is decrypted for inspection, scanned in parallel by the IPS engine and explicit web proxy, then re-encrypted and forwarded when clean or blocked with a replacement message when a threat is found.

The presenter configures a FortiProxy VM for a facilities organization: FortiGuard licensing and scheduled cloud updates, feature toggles, LDAP users and groups, and security profiles for category web filtering, application control with social-media blocks, DLP rules for HTTP methods and patterns, and AI-driven content analysis. An explicit-proxy policy ties these profiles to the facilities group, enables HTTP and HTTPS web caching, logging, and client PAC settings. Live tests show Facebook blocked under application control, YouTube and gambling and dating sites blocked by web filtering, an EICAR test file stopped by antivirus, a sample SSN download stopped by DLP, and weapon imagery replaced by the vendor logo under content analysis.

The close covers traffic and security logs with policy and threat detail, plus cache monitoring and WAN optimization. Practitioners gain a concrete picture of how one appliance enforces layered outbound web policies and what visibility operators get from session logs.

talks.title: FortiGate 3700F ULL Test Results | FortiGate
talks.teaser: Benchmarks show FortiGate 3700F ULL latency near one microsecond with 75 Gbps enterprise mix under full threat protection.
talks.summary:
The presentation positions the FortiGate 3700F as a compact data-center firewall for hybrid IT, with multiple 400 gigabit Ethernet links and four ultra-low-latency ports rated up to 25 gigabits per second—aimed at use cases such as online gaming, conferencing, and high-frequency trading where small packets must move with minimal delay.

The first demonstrations stress concurrent load. With Spirent’s SPT-N4U feeding both ultra-low-latency and 400G QSFP-DD ports, measured ULL latency stays near 1 to 1.18 microseconds average despite roughly 33 gigabits bi-directional on ULL and 239 gigabits bi-directional on 400G. Isolated RFC 2544-style runs with 64-byte traffic report ULL lows around 1.16 microseconds with 0.01 microsecond jitter at nearly 98.3 gigabits and about 153 million packets per second; 400G ports reach roughly 3.6 microseconds latency with 0.06 microsecond jitter under the same packet size.

A separate enterprise-mix scenario uses two Spirent Cyberflood C200 appliances with standard IPS, application control, antivirus, certificate inspection, and logging enabled. Throughput climbs to 75 gigabits per second inspected traffic at about 84% CPU with IPS engines at 95–97% utilization, running over five minutes with full transaction success. Practitioners should treat the numbers as lab outcomes tied to Spirent test gear and Fortinet’s stated security profile, useful for sizing latency-sensitive and high-throughput segmentation designs.

talks.title: Application Delivery Controller and GSLB | FortiADC
talks.teaser: Shows FortiADC's deployment options and a round-robin server load balancing demo across two web servers.
talks.summary:
This Fortinet video is a product overview of FortiADC, an application delivery controller that the presenter describes as a way to keep applications available, secure and optimized. It can run as a hardware appliance with a range of throughput tiers, as a virtual machine on several hypervisors, or as a cloud deployment on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle and Alibaba Cloud. The licensing options mentioned are bring-your-own licence, pay-as-you-go and subscription.

The presenter also introduces a DNS-based global server load balancing cloud service that aims to keep an application online during local traffic spikes or network downtime. The demo then moves into the management console, where a virtual server fronts a real server pool of two Apache web servers. The virtual server listens on HTTPS port 443, uses a source NAT pool and has no session persistence configured, so requests are distributed round robin.

Refreshing the browser shows each request alternating between the two backend servers, which the presenter uses to show that the traffic is being balanced. The video closes by positioning the product for enterprise networks, service providers, MSSPs and hybrid architectures, as a way to improve scalability, performance and security for applications hosted on premises or in the cloud.

talks.title: FortiFlex VMware License Provisioning Demo | FortiFlex
talks.teaser: Administrators see how FortiFlex provisions FortiGate VMs on VMware ESXi with on-demand entitlements and license tokens.
talks.summary:
The session introduces Fortinet’s Flex-VM program for deploying and licensing selected virtual appliance products. Enterprise customers and MSSPs can define license configurations and VM entitlements on demand through the support portal, without caps on instance count or vCPU sizing. FortiGuard, cloud, and support offerings tie to appliance size, account scope, VDOM or feature counts, and a points model sold as prepaid licenses or monthly post-paid usage for MSSPs.

Scalability and REST API automation are emphasized so entitlements can be resized as requirements change. The walkthrough uses post-paid FortiCloud Flex-VM access: a new service-bundle configuration named for VMware with one CPU, an Enterprise package, and four virtual domains, then a matching entitlement for two machines with month-end expiry. On ESXi, a FortiGate VM starts unlicensed until an operator copies the pending entitlement token, applies it via a console license command, and reboots.

After install, the appliance reports success, serial 1286 appears in the GUI as licensed, and the cloud portal marks that entitlement active. Practitioners learn the portal-to-hypervisor flow for binding tokens to running VMs and confirming license state on both sides.

talks.title: FortiFlex (formerly known as Flex-VM) Provisioning with AWS Demo | FortiFlex
talks.teaser: Demonstrates licensing a FortiGate VM on AWS EC2 through FortiFlex configurations and entitlements.
talks.summary:
This demo walks through licensing a FortiGate virtual machine running on an AWS EC2 instance using FortiFlex, the Fortinet service formerly called Flex-VM. The presenter starts with the instance already deployed and an SSH session open, then signs in to the Fortinet cloud portal to set up the license.

In the portal, a new FortiFlex configuration is created with a name, the FortiGate VM service bundle as the product type, two CPUs, the Enterprise service package, and zero virtual domains. A VM entitlement is then created against that configuration, with a user-defined expiration at the end of the month and a count of two virtual machines. Two entitlements are generated, and the presenter picks one of them and copies its license token.

Back on the FortiGate, the token is applied through the CLI license command. The GUI is then checked to confirm the license is active. The entitlement page shows the token as used, the status as active, and the termination date at the end of the month. The practical takeaway is a simple provisioning sequence: define the configuration, issue entitlements, apply each token to a device, and verify the result in the portal.

talks.title: Secure Access Demo | FortiSASE
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how FortiSASE enforces web, app, SaaS and private access policies through one cloud console.
talks.summary:
The demo presents FortiSASE, a cloud-delivered service that combines networking and security for a hybrid workforce, on or off the corporate network. It covers secure internet access, secure SaaS access and private application access. Web filtering blocks risky categories such as phishing, gambling and crypto mining, and deep SSL inspection is enabled for user traffic.

On the endpoint, the presenter confirms the client is managed by the cloud console, connected over an SSL VPN tunnel, and holding zero trust tags. Visits to a phishing site and a gambling site return block pages giving the reason, and WhatsApp is stopped by application control. For SaaS, tenant restrictions inserted through HTTP headers block personal Microsoft accounts while the corporate Office 365 tenant signs in via single sign-on, and app override rules block uploads to Box, Dropbox and personal Google Drive. For private access, split tunneling keeps internal subnet traffic off the VPN, and SD-WAN hubs linked by IPsec and BGP are chosen by priority and health. Access to an internal server and an SSH session through ZTNA are both gated by authentication.

The final section reviews web filter and application control logs, filtered by username and action. Blocked gambling and phishing events appear, and the Office 365 block is attributed to Microsoft acting on the injected headers. Private access logs show the SD-WAN rule and link quality for the internal server, while the SSH session is absent because it went directly to the access proxy. The takeaway is that one console sets web, SaaS and private access policies and shows what was enforced.

talks.title: How to Create a Event Correlation Rule | FortiSIEM
talks.teaser: Demonstrates turning a Windows brute-force logon search into a correlation rule and mapping it to the MITRE framework.
talks.summary:
The demo starts with a search for failed Windows logons, filtered on reporting devices and grouped by user, with an aggregation count showing how often the events occurred over a one-day window. The results list the reporting IP, user, event name and number of matches, and the presenter turns that search into a new rule from the action tab.

The rule is built from a sub-pattern made of the filter, the aggregation and the group-by fields. The presenter changes the aggregate threshold to five, sets the category to security and the subcategory to authentication, and selects brute-force password guessing as the technique. The action uses the sub-pattern and an incident title that includes the username variable. After saving, the rule is found in the resources section and activated.

Once the rule has fired, it appears in the incident list with details such as the username, reporting device, tactics and techniques. Expanding the entry shows the pattern conditions that were defined. The presenter then checks the MITRE incident coverage view, searches for brute-force password guessing, and confirms the new rule is listed under the matching framework category.

talks.title: Automation in 5G RAN and Edge Environments | MWC23
talks.teaser: A booth interview explains how automated edge security in 5G Open RAN test beds keeps latency and energy flat while traffic grows.
talks.summary:
Mobile World Congress segment revisits a joint Intel test bed focused on automation and security for 5G Open RAN and telecom edge deployments. The Fortinet and Enterprise Web participants frame security as foundational for carrier infrastructure and describe collaboration meant to protect applications and edge infrastructure without trading away the latency and efficiency goals operators expect.

They report demonstration results at scale where security posture, latency, and energy use stayed stable rather than spiking as load increased. They cite edge latency on the order of microseconds and note that when traffic rose, coordinated automation actually improved energy performance. The setup combines Intel infrastructure open APIs, AI-driven tuning inside Fortinet security applications for volatile traffic, and continuous co-optimization across service slice, RAN, core, and related management elements so quality of service stays steady.

Practitioners should take away that edge 5G security cannot live in silos. Modern offerings are composable stacks; securing them means orchestrating automation, APIs, and policy across RAN, core, and edge tiers so SLAs for performance, efficiency, and protection are met together.

talks.title: FortiGate CNF and FortiManager Integration | Product Demo
talks.teaser: A demonstration shows how FortiGate CNF on AWS links to FortiManager to deploy egress firewall rules and validate HTTP blocking in a VPC.
talks.summary:
The session introduces FortiGate CNF as a SaaS next-generation firewall aimed at cloud network security, especially egress traffic from cloud environments. The speaker outlines why growing cloud adoption raises concerns such as data exfiltration, malware spread, botnet activity, and high volumes of outbound traffic, and positions CNF as a way to enforce consistent policy across multiple cloud accounts while reducing the need to operate dedicated firewall infrastructure.

FortiGate CNF is described as running on AWS gateway instances with autoscaling, inspecting north-south and east-west traffic through policy sets, malware and IPS controls, web and DNS filtering, and dynamic address objects. Management can use the CNF console, AWS Firewall Manager, or FortiManager, with FortiGuard threat intelligence applied across hybrid and AWS deployments.

The demonstration focuses on FortiManager mode: enabling management during CNF creation, registering the active instance in Device Manager, then adding a policy ahead of the default allow rule to deny HTTP and HTTPS while permitting other traffic. With defaults in place, HTTP and VNC both pass; after the new policy is installed through the install wizard, HTTP is blocked while VNC still works, illustrating centralized policy push to the CNF instance.

talks.title: FortiSIEM Custom Dashboard Types and Use Cases | FortiSIEM
talks.teaser: Shows how to build FortiSIEM dashboards with summary, widget, and Sankey or link graph views.
talks.summary:
The video walks through building several dashboard types in FortiSIEM, starting with a new shared dashboard created inside a folder. A summary dashboard is introduced as a way to view real-time events and a health status overview, and it is populated with the devices already added to the system. The presenter then moves to widget dashboards, where each chart shows one metric from one source. Examples include the top network devices by CPU and memory utilization, the top devices by failed logins, and the top outbound ports by bytes.

The demonstration then changes how the same data is displayed. The failed-login chart is switched from a table to an aggregation view and then a donut view, with the time grouping set to hours, weeks or days. For firewall permit traffic, a filter on permitted events with source and destination fields first appears as a table, then becomes a Sankey chart showing flow from source to destination, and finally a link graph that shows the relationships between them.

To reuse that query, the presenter saves it as a report named demo dashboard in the ungrouped section and adds it back to the original dashboard as a widget. That widget is set to a Sankey chart, with options to choose the direction of the source and target fields. The main takeaway is that one saved query can be presented in several chart styles, so the dashboard type should match the question being answered.

talks.title: Speed Up Operations with AI-Powered Analytics and Automation | FortiSOC
talks.teaser: Shows how a Fortinet SOC product uses playbooks and event handlers to automate incident response across a security fabric.
talks.summary:
The session demonstrates how FortiAnalyzer and the FortiSOC module automate and orchestrate security response using built-in playbooks, event handlers and connectors for the Security Fabric. The presenter explains that threat intelligence packages are pushed to FortiAnalyzer, which can rescan historical logs for continuous detection, and that when ransomware or other malware activity is logged, matching playbooks and handlers fire automatically to contain it.

The walkthrough starts in the console. Device Manager shows real-time logging across fabric devices, and the monitors cover threat maps and top destinations, traffic with source and destination views, and ZTNA connection statistics. A list of compromised hosts on the demo network is shown. The SOC dashboards summarise playbook executions, incident counts and mitigated versus unhandled events by type. Event handlers are reviewed next: the Recon handler has 11 filters, the detection-by-threat handler has 15 filters covering risky domains and phishing, and outbreak alerts flag items such as Dark Side ransomware. In the demo, most malware events were mitigated by the malicious file detection handler.

Playbooks, built with drag-and-drop tasks and either enabled by default or created custom, run automatically when linked events occur, and their task-level status is tracked in a Playbook Monitor. The demo also covers a critical intrusion incident playbook and an incident being assigned, categorised and given extra playbooks by hand. The presenter closes by suggesting this automation reduces response time and total cost of ownership, and directs viewers to Fortinet for implementation details.

talks.title: FortiExtender Out of Band Management (OBM) Demo | 5G/LTE Security
talks.teaser: Shows FortiExtender's out-of-band management giving admins serial console access to remote devices when the primary link fails.
talks.summary:
The video presents the out-of-band management (OBM) feature of FortiExtender, a 4G and 5G cellular WAN gateway. It targets remote sites, such as a retail outlet or small branch office, that may have no local technical staff. When the primary connection fails, an administrator would otherwise face an eight-hour drive just to find the cause. OBM uses a built-in console server so the administrator can reach the equipment over the cellular link, which serves as an independent path.

The demo uses a lab remote site where the extender connects through a USB hub to three Fortinet devices via USB-to-RJ45 serial cables, none of them internet-connected. From the cloud management portal, which allows access from any location, the presenter opens the OBM prompt and chooses a serial port. Port 1 reaches the console of a FortiGate 40F, port 2 reaches a FortiGate 61F, and port 3 reaches a third device. From that console, an administrator can run diagnostic or troubleshooting commands. The presenter notes that serial connections also work with non-Fortinet equipment.

The talk closes by tying the feature to uptime and business continuity. The presenter argues that organizations deploying FortiExtender with OBM can expect less downtime, since administrators keep access to remote gear even when the main link is down. The practical takeaway is to plan console access for remote sites before an outage happens.

talks.title: 2H 2022 Threat Landscape Report | FortiGuardLIVE
talks.teaser: Reviews 2022 threat trends: early reconnaissance, wiper growth, recycled malware code and a prioritised red zone of exposures.
talks.summary:
This interview walks through the second-half 2022 threat landscape report from Fortinet's FortiGuard Labs. The discussion starts with attackers moving earlier in the kill chain. Cybercriminals study defenders and weaponise flaws quickly, as seen with Log4j and ProxyShell. The report's external exposure data covers leaked credentials, card data and exposed services, so organisations can act before initial access. Drive-by compromises are also highlighted, including cracked software pushed through search ads, along with heavy use of phishing and spear phishing.

The second part covers wipers. The speakers cite wiper families rising from 16 in the first half to 53 between Q3 and Q4, including disk and data wipers, and note open-source wipers appearing on GitHub. They argue that organisations of any size could be targeted. A new code analysis looks at Motet, where about 90 variants fall into six clusters. Shared code between variants shows reuse, while a variant with no shared code signals active development. Separating new code from old needs machine learning and automation, because detection signatures and model features depend on it.

The final part introduces the red zone, a funnel from the total attack surface, which includes almost 200,000 CVEs, to each organisation's open attack surface and then to the active attack surface attackers actually target. Only a small slice is under active exploitation, so the guest argues that patching should follow exploitation activity rather than severity alone. Each report section includes mitigation advice across the kill chain, including incident response and training.

talks.teaser: Covers a network engineer's path into cybersecurity and gives career advice for women entering the field.
talks.summary:
This career conversation pairs Renee Tarun, a deputy CISO, with Sarah Ryba, a senior network engineer at an MSP partner. Ryba describes her recent regional win in a hands-on competition where participants configure security fabric products against timed objectives. She credits her daily work with those products, plus the certification training behind them, for helping her handle features she had not used before.

The discussion then follows her route into the field. She started at 17 as a network technician, earned an associate's degree, and moved through networking into database administration. Working on data protection, where the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information matter most, sparked her interest in security. She stresses that career paths in IT are broad, so a clear goal and guidance from a mentor matter a great deal for newcomers.

Near the end, both speakers agree that continuing education and reading industry material keep skills current, and that stepping outside a comfort zone often produces the most growth. Ryba also says that even roles she did not want taught her planning, budgeting and lasting professional relationships. The session closes by pointing viewers to the training institute's pages for courses and career development.

talks.title: FortiGate CNF AWS Onboarding Tutorial | Cloud Security
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning FortiGate CNF AWS Onboarding Tutorial | Cloud Security.
talks.summary:
# Overview
This tutorial details the registration, initial account setup, and configuration process for FortiGate CNF (referred to in the transcript phonetically as 40K CNF / 40 OS / 40 Cloud). FortiGate CNF is a managed next-generation firewall (NGFW) offering that delivers network security for AWS Cloud environments, powered by FortiOS and FortiGuard Labs threat intelligence services.

# Key Topics
- Subscribing to FortiGate CNF through the AWS Marketplace.
- Creating and verifying a management account and registering user credentials.
- Linking an AWS account to FortiGate CNF using an AWS CloudFormation template stack.
- Creating a CNF instance and logging traffic to an Amazon S3 bucket.
- Configuring endpoints, subnets, and subnet tags within the AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).
- Establishing VPC route tables to direct north-south traffic through Gateway Load Balancer endpoints for inspection.

# Technical Details
1. **Marketplace & Registration**: Access the FortiGate CNF page on the AWS Marketplace, subscribe, and proceed to set up an account. Registration requires an email address, CAPTCHA verification, an email verification code, setting a secure password, submitting account details, and accepting contract terms before signing in.
2. **AWS Account Linking**: Inside the CNF management console, navigate to the AWS account menu to add an account by supplying the AWS Account ID. Launch the AWS Quick Create CloudFormation stack, acknowledge IAM resource creation, and wait for the stack status to reach `CREATE_COMPLETE`.
3. **Instance Creation**: In CNF Instances, create a new instance by specifying the CNF name, region, log type, and configuring traffic logging to an S3 bucket. Wait until the instance status transitions to active.
4. **Endpoint Configuration**: Under endpoints, create a new endpoint specifying the name, account, and VPC ID. Copy the key name `fortigate_subnet_type` (rendered phonetically as `for the gay _ subnet _ type` in transcript). In AWS VPC Subnet settings, add a tag with this key name and the value set to `endpoint`. Back in the CNF endpoint dialog, select the tagged subnet, finish configuration, and verify that the endpoint status changes to active in both the console and AWS.
5. **North-South Routing Deployment**: To inspect traffic, three dedicated route tables are created in the VPC:
   - `CNF-Ingress-workload`: Configured with destination `0.0.0.0/0` (represented as `0.0.0.0`) targeting the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (VPCE). This directs all outbound workload traffic (except local traffic) to FortiGate CNF.
   - `cnf-Ingress-internet`: Configured with the workload subnet as destination targeting the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (VPCE). This ensures incoming traffic from the internet passes through FortiGate CNF prior to reaching the VPC subnet.
   - `CNF-egress-igw`: Configured with destination `0.0.0.0/0` targeting the Internet Gateway (IGW) for external network traffic leaving the environment after traversing FortiGate CNF.

# Takeaways
FortiGate CNF integrates natively with AWS networking constructs using CloudFormation and Gateway Load Balancer endpoints. Proper north-south inspection requires configuring specific ingress and egress route tables in the VPC so traffic seamlessly forwards through the firewall instance before reaching destinations or exiting via the internet gateway. Users can consult the admin guide for additional architectures and workload options.

talks.title: Secure SD-WAN 7.2 Demo | SD-WAN
talks.teaser: Shows Fortinet Secure SD-WAN 7.2 covering branch provisioning, application steering, analytics, reporting and integrated security.
talks.summary:
A Fortinet product demo of Secure SD-WAN 7.2 starts by showing FortiManager as the central management and orchestration point, paired with FortiAnalyzer for logs and analytics under one console. The presenter builds a dual-hub overlay with a setup wizard, with an option to enable ADVPN for full mesh connectivity between branches. A third branch is then added using a device blueprint and a pre-authorized model device, so it onboards automatically once it comes online.

Path selection comes next. Members combine underlay and overlay interfaces, performance SLA health checks mix active probes with passive measurements from real application flows, and SLA rules steer traffic. Application steering can use the internet service database, which steers on first packet, or deep packet inspection for finer identification, with over 5,000 applications and custom signatures possible. Three strategies are shown: best quality, lowest cost with a metered cellular backup, and maximize bandwidth for active-active load balancing. Analytics include a global site map, per-site SLA charts, application bandwidth views, MOS scoring for calls, and log views and alerts, along with reporting templates.

The demo closes with security: enabling AV, IPS and SSL inspection on the firewall policy for local internet traffic, and cloud-delivered services for remote users that can join the overlay. It also covers managing FortiSwitch, FortiAP and FortiExtender from the same console. The takeaway is a single-vendor approach that ties branch networking, monitoring and security together.

talks.title: Threat Landscape for the Public Sector in 2023 | FortinetLIVE
talks.teaser: Outlines the 2023 threat landscape for state and local government, from ransomware and OT risk to staffing and automation gaps.
talks.summary:
This interview-style session looks at the threat landscape for state and local government heading into 2023. The speaker says ransomware remains the top worry for agencies, but attackers now add data wiping and extortion of citizens' personal information, so offline backups alone do not cover the risk. He counts roughly 15 larger ransomware-as-a-service operations, some staffed by 50 to 100 people, which brings more tactics and techniques. The blurred line between advanced persistent threat actors and criminal groups is also discussed.

Comparing government with the private sector, the speaker sees similar threats but a larger attack surface. Public bodies tend to lag on staffing and technology but do better on process, using frameworks such as zero trust. Governance is hard because a jurisdiction often cannot direct the organizations within it, and some local bodies have no IT staff at all. Operational technology is flagged as a growing risk, especially where IT and OT systems connect through integrations and APIs that attackers can use to break the chain.

For 2023 the speaker recommends earlier detection in the reconnaissance and weaponization phases, incident response planning, and asset management. Automated threat intelligence, orchestration with playbooks, SOC-as-a-service, deception and digital risk protection can help small teams keep up. Federal infrastructure funding is reaching state and local governments, but project management skills are a gap. The takeaway: smaller organizations should consume services or regionalize to reach the scale needed for monitoring.
